### 7.1 Corporate governance profile

During the reporting period, the Bank operated in line with the Company Law, Joint Stock Commercial Banks Corporate Governance Guidance, Joint-stock Commercial Banks Board of Director Duty Execution (Trial) and other documents, in addition to the Bank's Articles of Association, along with the Bank's current circumstances of constantly improving governance structure and internal control systems which ensure that shareholders, the Board of Directors, the Board of Supervisors, and senior management operate independently according to law, and fulfill their respective rights and obligations, without violating the laws and regulations.

The general meeting of shareholders is our most powerful vehicle. All shareholders exercise their rights through this meeting. The Board of Directors is responsible for arranging and holding the general meeting, and takes decisions on the Bank's major policies, development planning, employment and senior management income distribution. It does not however interfere with the Bank's specific transactions or management. The Board Chairman is its legal representative. The permanent organ of the Board of Directors is the Board of Directors' Office. The Board of Directors consists of a Strategic Committee, a Relevant Transaction Control Committee, a Risk Management Committee, a Nomination and Remuneration Committee, and an Audit Committee. These five special committees carry out duties under the leadership of the Board of Directors and report to the Board of Directors. The Board of Supervisors is responsible for the inspection and supervision of Board of Directors' and senior management due diligence, as well as significant financial and operational issues. The Bank implements a system in which the President assumes full responsibility under the leadership of the Board of Directors. The President has been appointed by the Board of Directors and reports thereto. The main duties of the President include organizing resolution implementation of the general shareholder meeting and Board of Directors, formulating the Bank's development planning and business plan program, formulating the Bank's internal management structure, managing the Bank's daily operations and so on. The Bank sets up and constantly improves the management system in which ownership and management, management and supervision separate from each other and balance interactively.

## 7.5 Meetings of special committees under the Board of Directors within the reporting period

During the reporting period, five special committees were set up under the Board of Directors, namely Strategy Committee, Related Party Transaction Committee, Risk Management Committee, Nomination and Remuneration Committee, and Audit Committee. Of which, the Strategy Committee held four meetings (including one voting by correspondence); Related Party Transaction Committee held four meetings; Risk Management Committee held voting by correspondence twice; Nomination and Remuneration Committee held four meetings; and the Audit Committee held voting by correspondence twice.

## 7.6 Legal requirements for independent directors

The Bank currently has one existent independent director. In 2010, the Board of Directors further strengthened the duty performance works of independent directors in accordance with the Articles of Association and related laws and regulations. Independent Director Jin Renshou, as Director Member of the Related Party Transaction Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee under the Board of Directors of the Bank, held a total of 8 meetings for the aforesaid two committees in accordance with laws and procedures, which meet the requirements of annual regular meetings. Independent Director Jin Renshou also presided over the duty performance evaluation of senior executives of the Bank, which was fully affirmed by the Board of Directors. Meanwhile, independent directors published independent and objective opinions respectively at the general meeting of shareholders, board meetings, and committees, in particular they made very constructive comments on development strategy, related transaction management, and personnel selection of our bank, playing an important role. In 2010, independent directors respectively conducted various research in newly-established branches including Qinzhou Branch, Beihai Branch, etc., many times, and proposed constructive comments for the Board of Directors and Business Management.

### Annual remuneration

广西北部湾银行股份有限公司2010年年度报告

## 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

## 8.1 Remuneration management structure and decision-making procedures of the bank

The Bank established a scientific and reasonable compensation management organizational structure in accordance with the remuneration management mode of a joint-stock commercial bank. The Board of Directors of the Bank is responsible for the remuneration management system and policy design and undertakes ultimate responsibility for remuneration of management. The Board of Directors decides the remuneration of senior executives, makes initial drafts for remuneration of directors and independent Directors, and submits them to the General Meeting of Shareholders for deliberation. At the beginning of each year, the Board of Directors approves the budgets for staff costs of the Bank.

## 8.2 The total annual remuneration and structure distribution

The Nomination and Remuneration Committee, under the Board of Directors, is responsible for drawing up the evaluation and compensation programs for directors, supervisors, and senior management personnel in terms of remuneration management, proposing suggestions to Board of Directors, and supervising the supervision program; evaluating the performance and remuneration level of senior management personnel of the Bank and supervising and reviewing the performance and remuneration level evaluations of other senior management personnel of the Bank. Currently the Bank's Nomination and Remuneration Committee has three members, namely Jin Renshou (Independent Director), Liu Jianping (Executive Director), and Ma Zhijun (Non-Executive Director). The Director Member is Independent Director Jin Renshou.

In 2010, annual remuneration totaled 242.9 million yuan. The remuneration structure is as follows: fixed remuneration is 71.4 million yuan, accounting for 29%; variable remuneration is 128.81 million yuan, accounting for 53%; and welfare income is 42.69 million yuan, accounting for 18%.

## 8.3 Measurement and risk adjustment of remuneration and performance

The Bank implements a performance-oriented remuneration management system, signs performance contracts with specific requirements for performance and risk, and confirms performance remuneration according to assessment results.

## 8.4 Deferred payment of remuneration

Deferred payment is implemented for 40% of the performance remuneration of business management of branches and employees whose positions have an important impact on risk, and for 50% of performance remuneration for main principals. Deferred payment is made in equal amounts within three years after assessment.

## 8.6 Formulation of the annual remuneration plan and completion of various indicators

The annual remuneration scale of the Bank is prepared, according to staff in the current year, expense budget, business development objectives, and annual salary scale expected increase, and submitted to the Board of Directors and General Meeting of Shareholders for deliberation. The remuneration scale in that year is ultimately determined according to the resolutions of the Board of Directors and General Meeting of Shareholders.

In 2010, the Bank's business underwent considerable development and profitability continued to improve, achieving synchronous development of scale, quality and efficiency. As at the end of 2010, the Bank's total assets amounted to 59.035 billion yuan, with a year-on-year increase of 31.836 billion yuan, up by 117.05%; the deposit balance amounted to 34.156 billion yuan, with a year-on-year increase of 10.733 billion yuan, up by 45.82%; and net profit after provision amounted to 439 million yuan, with a year-on-year increase of 242 million yuan, up by 122.84%. Capital adequacy ratio was 16.98%, with a year-on-year decrease of 5.36%; non-performing loan rate was 0.98%, with a year-on-year decrease of 0.54%; and loan coverage ratio was 217.71%, with a year-on-year increase of 56.55%. Total remuneration of senior executives in 2010 amounted to 3.84 million yuan, with a year-on-year decrease of 3.57 million yuan. Completion indicators of the Bank was sound and implementation of remuneration was not contrary to performance and risk management of the Bank.

8.7 In 2010, the Bank had no exceptions beyond the original remuneration plan.

Comprehensive risk management

广西北部湾银行股份有限公司2010年年度报告

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

### 9.1 Overall assessment of risk management in 2010

In 2010, the Bank steadily promoted risk management and operated the comprehensive risk management system in an orderly manner. The risk awareness and awareness of compliance of the management were constantly enhanced. At the beginning of the year, the Bank identified risk management for 2010, with "basic risk management year" with the aim of, creating value through risk management as the concept, and "laying a solid basis for risk control and innovative management measures" as the goal, formulated and issued the Opinions of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Guidance of Risk Management of 2010, clarified four major risk management objectives and specific measures to be adopted, and clarified risk management objectives and work focuses of the Bank in 2010, having laid a sound foundation for risk management throughout the year, having led risk management orientation of the Bank, and having promoted continuous and stable development of various businesses.

As of the end of 2010, the balance of our Bank's various deposits was 34.155 billion yuan and loan balance was 17.202 billion yuan, with a respective increase of 10.711 billion yuan and 3.867 billion yuan over the previous year, respectively, up by 45.73% and 29%, and the term-end loan-to-deposit ratio was 50.4%; non-performing loan balance was 169 million yuan and non-performing loan ratio was 0.98%, respectively down by 33.94 million yuan and 0.54 percentage points compared with the end of the previous year. In terms of credit risk, the amount of non-performing loan and the non-performing loan ratio decreased; in terms of market risk, interest rate in the second half increased and changes in interest rates imposed higher requirements on the Bank's portfolio and trading; in terms of operational risk, excepting certain risks in payment, settlement, credit and other business operations, there were no significant operational risk loss events or incidents during the report period; and in terms of liquidity risk, monitoring and management of liquidity ratio indicators performed well, maintaining a good liquidity. ### 9.2.2 Non-performing loans

### 9.2.3 Changes in major risk points

At the end of 2010, the Bank's balance of non-performing loans amounted to 169.36 million yuan, down by 33.93 million yuan over the beginning of the year; non-performing loan rate was 0.98%, down by 0.54 percentage points from the beginning of the year, having enacted "double reduction" in non-performing loans.

(1) Large client concentration. The number of the Bank's corporate customers with a loan balance over 50 million yuan totaled 71. Loans totaled 8.891 billion yuan, accounting for 62.84% of the balance of corporate loans and accounting for 51.69% of total loans of the Bank; number of clients with balance of loans over 100 million yuan totaled 39. Loans totaled 6.774 billion yuan, accounting for 47.88% of balance of all corporate loans and accounting for 39.38% of total loans of the bank. The proportion of large-amount loans over 50 million yuan to loans of the Bank decreased by 9.94 percentage points from 61.63% at the beginning of the year; and the proportion of large-amount loans over 100 million yuan to loans of the Bank decreased by 9.67 percentage points from 49.05% at the beginning of the year. The situation of large-loan client concentration was significantly improved.

(2) Industry concentration. At the end of the reporting period, the proportion of corporate loans for the top five industries to total loans was 80.3%, of which the proportions of loans for manufacturing, real estate, transportation, storage and postal industry and for water conservancy, environmental and public facilities management industry decreased to different extents, having made certain achievements in restructuring the credit industry. Especially, the balance of real estate loans decreased by 321.0318 million yuan over the beginning of the year and the proportion dropped over 6.05 percentage points from the beginning of the year.

(3) Credit customer structure. At the end of the year, in 17.202 billion yuan of loan, corporate customers accounted for 82.25% and personal loans accounted for 17.75%. The proportion of personal loans rose by 4.29 percentage points from the beginning of the year, with the customer credit structure being further optimized.

(4) Loan term structure. By comparative analysis of year-end loan term structure, loans with a term exceeding one year accounted for 65.20% and medium-term and long-term loans accounted for over half of the total loans of the Bank. Attention should be paid to increasing medium-term and long-term loans and a combination of credit terms should be reasonably allocated.

### 9.2.4 Key management initiatives

(1) Strengthen the basic framework of the credit system and enhance the quality and efficiency of credit operations.

① Issued the Guidance of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank for Credit Policy and Structural Adjustment for 2010, clarified the controls orientation for 2010 from several dimensions including client, industry, region and product, confirmed the general guiding ideology and philosophy for strengthening the credit infrastructure, adjusting and solidifying the basic risk management policy, and guided the directions of the credit business of the Bank throughout the year. And for real estate, government financing platform and the "two high and one left" industry loan, formulated the list of customers for compression and exit, and promoted optimal adjustment of the credit structure.

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

② Sorted out the credit rules and regulations, completed the overall clean-up of the credit system of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank since the establishment.

☐ Further improved the credit system construction and provided a strong guarantee for the institutional and standardized operation of the credit business.

(2) Further improved the management mechanisms of risk managers and optimized the presence of risk managers.

(3) Organized the implementation of joint examinations after lending and strengthened collateral file management.

① After the implementation of a joint examination mechanism on a quarterly basis ensured timely notification.

② Set up a collateral monitoring center, mobilized personnel to conduct on-site tracking and inspection of the collateral supervision unit in the governing area of Nanning for timely detection and prevention risk control.

③ Paid close attention to the standard management of credit files, file storage by the Bank throughout the year is 99%, increased, this is up by 30 percentage points from 69% over the previous year end. Meanwhile, the pass rate of credit files rose from 50% to 85.20%.

(4) Strengthened post-loan inspection, supervision and rectification work and strictly regulated access of the agency management.

① First, organized a special inspection of the implementation of "three measures and one guidance" promulgated by the CBRC. Second, assisted in on-site inspection of fixed asset project loans and examination of the authenticity of the bill trade background, urged the implementation of rectification measures in relevant branches for problems detected, and made reports to the office of China Banking Regulatory Commission. Third, conducted a special inspection of real estate projects, loans of government investment and financing platform, and loans of Tiandong Village Bank. Fourth, in 2009, implemented the rectification of problems found in three on-site inspections carried out by the CBRC and Guangxi Office, CBRC, urged all relevant branches, departments and offices to implement rectifications, and regularly reported such rectifications to the CBRC and Guangxi Office, CBRC; currently all relevant branches, departments and offices have completed rectifications.

(5) Innovated various manners of risk control management and effectively enhanced the levels of risk management.

② Did a good job in the access management of movable charges mortgage monitoring and promoted business development.

Implemented the risk early warning system. Made risk warnings and disclosures in a timely manner for potential risks in business operations and in the management process of the relevant management departments of branches and head office, issued a total of 7 copies of risk warnings, and took timely risk prevention action.

(6) Made strict assessments of credit management and improved the quality and efficiency of the work.

Organized credit evaluations and made comprehensive evaluation notifications to the bank on credit performance objectives, credit management objectives, credit management quality and efficiency, and other works of the ten branches within the administrative area on a quarterly basis. On one hand, by revealing deficiencies and pointing out the gaps, we enhanced the credit management capacity of the branches; on the other hand, we provided a reference basis for the future implementation of differential management policy of the head office.

(7) Actively promoted the compression reduction of non-performing loans and disposal of recovered assets.

With regard to compression reduction of non-performing loans, first, seriously organized and conducted classification of the five categories of assets and objectively reflected the true state of credit assets; second, made a well-developed compression reduction program for non-performing loans, adopted legal proceedings to collect non-performing loans from clients with poor willingness to pay back, and promptly implemented, or enhanced the implementation of, procedures for filing; third, dealt with risk loans through increasing loan collateral and other means. 100 million yuan of principal and interest was collected through the year in cash. At the end of the year, "double reduction" was realized in respect of non-performing loans and the non-performing loan rate. With regard to the disposal of recovered assets, as at the end of 2010, the head office successfully collected 902 million yuan, accounting for 73.87% of 1.221 billion yuan of non-performing loans. Through the maintenance of owner equity, the Bank increased both the net amount of the Bank's capital and the anti-risk ability.

(8) Carry out various forms of training and create a good credit team.

First, a total of 492 people participated in the credit post exam and the pass rate was 94.12%; second, successfully held the "three measures and one guidance" through the "credit business knowledge contest"; third, actively organized participation in the knowledge competition of "three measures and one guidance" held by the China Banking Industry Association, winning No. 4 place for individuals and No. 2 place for groups in Guangxi District, and winning No. 3 place for groups in a contest in Chengdu on behalf of Guangxi; fourth, participated in and organized supply chain financing, collateral regulation, and other external studies, learning from advanced experiences of other banks to promote the development of this Bank; fifth, organized a series of training activities on post-loan management, credit assets risk classification, file management, corporate credit risk points and countermeasures, credit system operation, credit line assessment, "three measures and one guideline", etc., in total training over 600 people.

### 9.3 Market risk

#### 9.3.1 Interest rate risk

The central bank raised the benchmark deposit and lending interest rates, so the deposit and lending interest rate yield curve was smooth, and the potential impact on the Bank's deposit and loan portfolio is not clear. The potential impact of changes in interest rates on capital investment of the Bank's treasury department is large. At the end of the year, the main investment holdings of the Bank's capital department are respectively: 2.466 billion yuan of trading financial assets, 2.839 billion yuan of held-to-maturity investment, 2.334 billion yuan of available-for-sale financial assets, and 9.052 billion yuan of bonds purchased under resale agreements.

#### Including:

(1) Held-to-maturity investment products total 15, primarily trust wealth management investment and bank wealth management investment whose date of maturity is within six months and the overall interest rate risk is not significant;

(2) Available-for-sale financial assets products total 25, mainly local enterprise bonds, policy bank bonds and commercial bank bonds, with maturity of over 5 years. Because of rising interest rates in the second half year, the valuation of net bond value presented a declining trend.

(3) Trading financial assets products total 53, mainly corporate bonds, central bank bills and some national debt. Rise in interest rates twice in the fourth quarter caused changes in market interest rates and market interest rate fluctuations imposed a certain impact on the return from trading financial assets of the Bank. At the end of the year, the Capital Department made a valuation of trading financial assets and discovered a reduction in carrying fair value of 16.3891 million yuan.

(4) Financial assets purchased under resale agreements consist primarily of reverse bonds repurchased and bonds held on behalf of which: balance of reverse bonds repurchased is 592 million yuan and bond hold on behalf is 8.46 billion yuan, accounting for 6.54% and 93.46% respectively. Reverse bonds repurchased and bonds held on behalf are all short-term business, generally less than one month, with locked yield and less market risk.

#### 9.3.2 Exchange rate risk

At the end of the reporting period, the Bank's net foreign exchange exposure was 52,400 USD, equivalent to 326,400 yuan; structured exposure was 5,0059 million dollars, equivalent to 33,1526 million yuan, being foreign exchange working capital. In the fourth quarter of 2010, upon adjustment by the foreign exchange bureau, the Bank's consolidated position of foreign exchange settlement amount was 1 to 5 million USD. Foreign exchange settlement and sales businesses of the Bank could be completed in a timely manner locking the exchange rate risk, with foreign exchange settlement and sales exposure controlled within the amount approved by the foreign exchange bureau.

During the reporting period, the Bank did not carry out foreign exchange trade and had no foreign exchange exposure. No financial instruments of foreign exchange investment occurred. Within the year, the Bank only had foreign exchange settlement and sales services, without proprietary foreign exchange trades or hedging foreign exchange transactions. Overall exchange rate risk is minimal.

#### 9.3.3 Key management initiatives

(1) Strengthen risk monitoring and early warning, to ensure the healthy development of the business. In 2010, with the rapid growth of the Bank's capital investment business, risk management department strengthened monitoring and early warning of market risk, combined with macroeconomic policy direction, and made a dynamic monitoring analysis of the investment business and structure of the Capital Department, led the Business Department to prudently master risk control, and promoted the healthy development of the business.

(2) The management made efforts to increase the identification, measurement and prevention capacities of market risk. By the use of duration and interest rate sensitivity analysis and other methods, the Bank makes duration calculations of bond investment over one year and analyzes the potential risk of change in the market value of bond investments with changing interest rate. In combination with interest rate movements, the Bank has a grasp of the Bank's bond investment structure to make constructive suggestions and to prevent interest rate risk.

(3) Formulate relevant systems, to lay a foundation for the introduction of new varieties of products. In 2010, the Bank formulated the Detailed Rules on the Implementation of Foreign Exchange Funds Trading Risk Management and Internal Control, laying a regulation foundation for gradual implementation of on-site and off-site foreign exchange trade in the industry.

### 9.4.2 Analysis of changes in the main risk indicators

(1) Liquidity ratio at the end of 2010, the Bank's liquidity ratio was 48.26%, down by 0.33 percentage points compared with the beginning of the year, but higher than the recommended liquidity ratio for small and medium banks, the warning level is not less than 30%.

(2) Liquidity gap ratio. At the end of 2010, the Bank liquidity gap was 1.41%, down by 52.92 percentage points compared with the beginning of the year. Although the decrease is large, it is still higher than the regulatory requirement of higher than or equal to -10%, the regulatory standard. The main reason is that in the case of controllable risk, in this year the Bank took the initiative to increase liabilities to enlarge the capital operation to improve the return on investment. The gap between liquid assets due within three months and liquid liabilities due within three years decreases. The liquidity gap ratio will decline quarterly and the year-end projected index is within the acceptable range.

(3) Core debt dependence. At the end of 2010, the Bank's dependence on core debt was 42.52%, 17.48 percentage points lower than the regulatory standard and down by 3.46 percentage points from the beginning of the year. It declined mainly because of the steady growth in deposits and a gradual increase in time deposit. But the bank borrowed large amounts of money from capital market for capital operations to earn the price difference in this year, leading to growth of time deposits lower than growth of total liabilities of the Bank (total liabilities amounted to 54.895 billion yuan, up by 30.916 billion yuan over the beginning of the year, up 128.93%) and resulting in a decline in the core liability dependence over the beginning of the year. Capital borrowed reduced the Bank's core deposit dependence and also improved its operating income and net income, further improving the Bank's capital profit margin and other profitability indicators.

With regard to secondary indicators of liquidity risk, the excess reserve ratio dropped by 5.1 percentage points over the beginning of the year, mainly because the Bank's Capital Department in this year increased the intensity of investment wealth management with financial products, while the central bank during the year raised the deposit reserve 6 times, a raise of 3 percentage points over the whole year, part of the excess reserves were transferred to statutory reserve and stored excess reserves decreased. At the end of December, the Bank's excess reserve balance was 2.353 billion yuan, down by 606 million yuan from the beginning of the year; the excess reserve rate was 7.53%, down by 5.1 percentage points over the beginning of the year.

### 9.4.3 Key management initiatives

(1) Formulate annual plan of liquidity risk management and clarify the focus of liquidity risk management throughout the year to ensure the safety of the Bank's liquidity.

(2) Adhere to a daily reporting system of liquidity, conduct dynamic monitoring of liquidity and capital flows, ensure secure payments and the normal operation of business, and maintain liquidity ratio within the level required by the regulators.

(3) Regularly carry out the Bank's liquidity risk analysis, make liquidity risk pressure test on the presumption of rising deposit reserve rates and continued loss of deposit, conduct individual tests by cash flow method at mild, moderate, and severe stress scenarios, measure cash inflow and outflow in each period, check if there is any short-term cash flow gap, and provide forward-looking judgments and decisions to strengthen the Bank's liquidity risk management.

(4) Strengthen coordination and communication between departments to ensure the liquidity of the Bank at no less than the warning line. For reasonable balance between liquidity and profitability, in 2010, the Bank further increased the monitoring of liquidity indicators; the relevant departments paid common attention to liquidity and deposit changes, and regrouped funds in case of pressure, to ensure the Bank's liquidity ratio at no less than 33%.

## 9.5 Operation risk

### 9.5.1 General condition

In 2010, the Bank attached great importance to operational risk management, carried out theme activities covering "internal control and prevention year," "Solid compliance foundation," and "service promoting development" in the bank, in combination with the requirements of the China Banking Regulatory Commission on case ruling, did a good job in risk elimination in all business in a comprehensive and multi-levelled manner, implemented improvement in cases of problems found in inspection, carried out system rearrangement, supplement, and improvement, enhanced staff training and counselling, and created a good compliance environment, further improving the Bank's operational risk management and controls. During the year, the Bank had no operational risk loss events or cases, but with the gradual expansion of business varieties and scope and increase in business volume, the occurrence frequency and total amount involved showed a gradual upward trend in general. Through the self-examination of branches and special inspections of functional departments and business lines of the head office, general operational risk events in the year totaled around 1610, involving 1.577 billion yuan; compared with the same period last year, operational risk events increased by 399 and the risk amount involved decreased by 2.755 billion yuan.

### 9.5.2 Key management initiatives

(1) The management seriously implemented the requirements of the China Banking Regulatory Commission and led the organization of "Internal control and prevention year". Since June 2010, the Bank has actively carried out the "internal control and prevention year". Over a period of more than six months, the activity covered the preparation phase, learning phase, self-examination and correction stage, supervision and inspection stage, and improvement stage. The Bank planned to issue five guidance documents for the "implementation year" with 9 guidance opinions. Leaders of the bank convened 6 work seminars and organized over 1500 employees for an internal control and prevention test. The Bank organized an Essay Competition for the "implementation year" and organized experts to participate in 3 seminars. The Bank identified and modified over 900 problems and modified more than 30 rules. The Bank issued a series of work incentive rules for internal control and prevention. Good results were achieved through the activity.

(2) Sort out rules and regulations and standardize operating procedures. For the credit business line, the Bank organized nearly 200 credit system correction and improvement works, introduced about 40 new credit system files covering Interim Measures on Management of Working Capital Loans, Interim Measures on Personal Loans, etc., and modified a series of SME credit rules; for the operating line, the Bank formulated 8 rules and operational measures including Reporting System of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Major Incidents, and resolved, supplemented, and improved 40 operation system, process, and operation measures (detailed rules) involving personnel management, account management, system management, authorization management, and monitoring management, to meet the development needs of the business. Through system improvement, the Bank has laid a solid foundation for internal control and supervision.

(3) Organized the implementation of a variety of system checks and enhanced risk prevention capacity.

## 9.6 Information technology risk

(4) Enhanced staff education and training, and improved the quality and skills of the staff.

In 2010, the Bank, around the information technology strategic priority and action plan of "perfecting information system and improve management service" to ensure stable operation of core business systems, comprehensively promoted information technology with system construction as the aim and realized no secure operation accidents in the year, business continuity of 100%, and no information technology risk events. Meanwhile, the Bank's information technology risk management capability was gradually improved and strengthened. Mainly reflected in:

(1) The Bank built an information technology management organization system. According to the requirements of the Guidance of the China Banking Regulatory Commission on Management of Information Technology Risk of Commercial Banks, the Bank set up the Information Technology Management Committee composed of senior management, information technology department and principals of main functional departments. The establishment of the Information Technology Management Committee will ensure improved information technology governance and enhanced risk management capacity, and will also ensure that the Bank's information technology plan is consistent with its overall development strategy and significant internal strategies.

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

(2) The Bank initially built three lines of defense to enhance risk control. To effectively prevent the risks that arise from information technology, the Information Technology Department, Risk Management Department and Audit Department strengthened communication and interaction, initially building the first defense of information technology running guarantee systems and an application restoration guarantee system composed of the Information Technology Department and Business Management Department; the second defense of risk identification, assessment, monitoring, improvement, and removing security risks in a timely manner, ensuring continuous running of business systems composed of Risk Management Department; and the third defense of post-control composed of external and internal audit departments supervising the implementation of information technology risk management and safeguarding IT risk control systems.

(3) The information technology risk system was further improved. According to the Guidance on Management of Information Technology Risk for Commercial Banks, Standard on Emergency Management of Important Information System for Banking Industry (Trial), Measures on Management of Production of and Change in Important Information System of Financial Institutions in the Banking Industry, Guidance on Regulation of Data Center of Commercial Bank, and other regulatory provisions of the China Banking Regulatory Commission, the Bank supplemented and improved the existing rules on management of information technology and operation, and formulated 12 rules covering the Detailed Rules of On-site Inspection of Information Technology Risk of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank (Interim) and Control Procedures on Computer Software Development Outsourcing of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank, etc.

(4) System building was accelerated, which strongly supported the business development. In 2010, the Bank set up 8 information technology system projects: credit card system, electronic commercial bill system, human resources system, the second generation of payment systems, electronic bank-enterprise reconciliation system, off-site audit system, call center system and electronic payment system of online banking. After a year of unremitting efforts, the construction of these systems has been basically completed and they have been launched for trial operation. Credit card system, electronic commercial bill system, the second generation of payment system, electronic payment system of online banking, and call center system have expanded channels of customer service and improved the Bank's competitiveness. The human resources system, electronic bank-enterprise reconciliation system, and off-site audit system have improved the information management mode of the Bank, partially realized electronic management, and improved working efficiency.

## 9.7 Main disadvantages

(1) The concentration of large-loan clients has declined, but the concentration ratio is still high. The number of the Bank's corporate customers with a balance of loans over 50 million yuan totaled 71. Loans totaling 8.891 billion yuan, accounting for 62.84% of the balance of corporate loans and accounting for 51.69% of the total loans of the Bank; the balance increased by 673 million yuan over the beginning of the year, but the share dropped by 8.37 percentage points from the beginning of the year; the number of clients with a balance of loans over 100 million yuan totaled 39. Loans totaled 6.774 billion yuan, accounting for 47.88% of the balance of all corporate loans and accounting for 39.38% of the total loans of the bank; the loan amount increased by 233 million yuan over the beginning of the year, but the ratio decreased by 8.8 percentage points from the beginning of the year. Overall, the proportion of loans for large clients is still relatively high.

(2) The presence of risk managers remains to be strengthened. In 2010, 40 positions were prepared for risk managers but only 26 were in place, this is not conducive to good post-loan management and the promotion of pilot parallel operations of risk managers in the future.

(3) Lack of market risk management is not conducive to good risk analysis and monitoring. Currently, the Bank has experienced market risk management and investment analysts, to restrict market risk through analysis, management, and monitoring.

(4) Market risk and liquidity risk management tools and instruments are limited and some business processes are to be optimized. At this stage, the Bank's market risk and liquidity risk management is mainly based on manual operation and analysis. The efficiency, accuracy and effectiveness is not high enough or strong enough. Improving the market risk and liquidity risk management level relies on the building of an information system. With regard to the business process, the Bank process of classified approval for financial instruments is too complicated, which adversely affects efficiency, therefore the system needs to be further revised and optimized.

(5) Relevant internal risk control measures on new business and new products are to be improved. With development of the Bank's investment banking, trade finance, foreign exchange and other new businesses, related internal risk control procedures and policies need to be supplemented and improved to ensure the healthy and orderly operation of new businesses and new products.

(6) With regard to information technology risk management, the coverage rate of contingency plans is still not high, outsourcing of risk management system is not perfect, and there is a lack of "Technical Support" personnel at some branches.

Corporate social

responsibility

广西北部湾银行股份有限公司2010年年度报告

### 10.1 The Bank's engagement in public welfare cases during the reporting period

(1) To support drought-control and earthquake relief in disaster-driven areas, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank organized the donation ceremony of "Beibu Gulf Bank in Action for Drought-control and Earthquake Relief" and donated a total of 110,000 yuan in total. At the same time, as an active response to the invocation of party committees at higher level and relevant departments, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank donated two "loving water tank" to Dashi mountainous area, a seriously drought-stricken area in Guangxi, to make its contribution to reconstruction after disaster.

(2) Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank plans to donate 2 million yuan over two years to medical research for people in Guangxi and for Chinese medical education in Guangxi. In 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank donated 1 million yuan to Guangxi Medical Education Foundation and the remaining funds will be donated in 2011.

(3) Qinzhou Branch, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank founded the "Love Education Fund" to which employees successively donated nearly 40,000 yuan, to support five students in tuition and living expenses. The Fund has enabled six students with financial difficulties to be admitted to university. Meanwhile, it established a long-term partnership with the "Social Concern" column of Qinzhou TV Station in order to provide assistance to poor students in a better manner.

## 10.2 Honors won during the reporting period

In April 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank won the titles of the "60 Most Influential Brands in Guangxi Since the Founding of New China" and "Faithful Enterprise in Guangxi".

In May 2010, it won the title of "World Expo China Year. Brand Bank with Faithful Services in China".

In July 2010, it won the titles of "Outstanding Enterprises in Guangxi in 2010" and "Top 100 Enterprises in Guangxi in 2010".

In August 2010, it won the titles of the "Most Promising Commercial Bank in China" and the "Top Ten Commercial Bank Providing Special Services".

In September 2010, it won the title of "Faithful China Seven Star Award" the Top Ten Most Trusted Brand in China for 2010.

#### Report of the Auditors

To the Board of Directors of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd

We have audited the accompanying financial statements of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd ("the Bank") and its subsidiary (collectively referred to as the "Group"), which comprise the consolidated and company balance sheets as at 31 December 2010, and the consolidated and company income statements, the consolidated and company cash flow statements and the consolidated and company statements of changes in shareholders' equity for the year then ended and notes to these financial statements.

##### Management's responsibility for the financial statements

The management of the Bank is responsible for the preparation of the financial statements in accordance with the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises. This responsibility includes:

(1) Designing, implementing and maintaining internal control relevant to the preparation of financial statements that are free from material misstatement, whether due to fraud or error;

(2) Selecting and applying appropriate accounting policies; and

(3) Making accounting estimates that are reasonable in the circumstances.

##### Auditor's Responsibility

Our responsibility is to express an opinion on these financial statements based on our audit. We conducted our audit in accordance with the China Standards on Auditing. Those standards require that we comply with ethical requirements and plan and perform the audit to obtain reasonable assurance as to whether the financial statements are free from material misstatement.

We believe that the audit evidence we have obtained is sufficient and appropriate to provide a basis for our audit opinion.

##### Opinion

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

##### GENERAL INFORMATION

Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd ("the Bank"), previously known as "Nanning City Cooperative Bank" or "Nanning City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd", is a local joint stock commercial bank established in March 1997 by transforming 17 Nanning City Credit Unions with the approval from People's Bank of China ("PBOC"). The former name of Nanning City Cooperative Bank was changed to another name of Nanning City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd in accordance with Guiyinfa [1998] No.67 issued by PBOC Guangxi Branch on 31 March 2008 and Nanyinfuzi [1998] No. 60 issued by PBOC Nanning Branch on 3 September 1998. According to "Approval of change of the name of Nanning City Commercial Bank" (Yinjianfu [2008] No. 405) issued by China Banking Regulatory Committee ("CBRC") on 10 October 2008, and "Approval of Establishment of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd" (Guizhenghan [2008] No.195) issued by the Government of Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region on 22 October 2008, the former name of Nanning City Commercial Bank Co., Ltd has been replaced by the current name of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd.

The original paid-in capital of the Bank upon establishment was RMB 110,655,000 and was verified by Guangxi Gongcheng CPA Firm with the issuing of the capital verification report (Chengyanzi [1997] No.23). The Bank increased its paid-in capital by RMB 29,000,000 and RMB 90,000,000 during the year 2004 and 2006, respectively, through issuing the new shares and the increased paid-in capital was verified by Zhongtianyin CPA Firm with the issuing of the capital verification reports (Zhongtianyin [2004] No.276 and Zhongtianyin [2006] No.663). In 2008, with the approval of Guiyinjianfu [2008] No.98 promulgated by CBRC Guangxi Bureau, the Bank received additional paid-in capital of RMB 1,770,345,000 through the issuing of new shares. As a result, the total registered capital was increased to RMB 2,000,000,000, which was verified by CPA Firms.

The Bank is registered as a business enterprise with Guangxi Administration for Industry and Commerce No. (Qi)450000000004866 and is licensed as a financial institution by CBRC Guangxi Bureau No. B0349H245010001.

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

The business scope of the Bank mainly includes: deposit taking from customers; granting of short, medium and long-term loans; domestic settlement; bills discounting; issuance of financial bonds; agent for issuance, settlement and sale of government bonds; trading in government bonds; placement with other banks; providing of guarantee; agent for collection of debtors; agent for signing of insurance contracts; safekeeping vault; entrusted loan for local finance bureau and other businesses as approved by CBRC.

By the end of 31 December 2010, the Bank has established 9 tier 1 branches, 2 county sub-branches, 49 tier 2 sub-branches, 60 operating outlets (60 opened). The registered address is 10 Qingxiu Road, Nanning City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

In 2009, the bank, together with other shareholders established Tiandong Beibu Gulf County Bank ("Tiandong County Bank", Note 6.9). The bank, together with Tiandong County Bank is called "The Group" or "Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Group".

The consolidated financial statements have been authorised for issue by the management of the Bank on 29 March 2011.

## 2 BASIS OF PREPARATION

The financial statements have been prepared in accordance with the Basic Standard and 38 specific standards of the Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises issued by the Ministry of Finance on 15 February 2006, and the Application Guidance for Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises, Interpretation of Accounting Standards for Business Enterprises and other relevant regulations issued thereafter (hereafter referred to as "the Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises" or "CAS").

## 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

### STATEMENT OF COMPLIANCE WITH THE ACCOUNTING STANDARDS FOR BUSINESS ENTERPRISES

The financial statements of the Group and the Bank for the year ended 31 December 2010 truly and completely present the financial position as at 31 December 2010 and the operating results, cash flows and other information for the year then ended of the Group and the Bank in compliance with the Accounting Standard for Business Enterprises.

## 4 PRINCIPAL ACCOUNTING POLICIES AND ACCOUNTING ESTIMATES

### 4.1 Principal accounting policies

#### 4.1.1 Accounting period

The Group's accounting year starts on 1 January and ends on 31 December.

4.1.2 Preparation of consolidated financial statements

The scope of consolidation includes the Bank and all of its subsidiaries.

Subsidiary is fully consolidated from the date on which control is transferred to the Group and is de-consolidated from the date that control ceases.

The financial statements of subsidiaries are adjusted in accordance with the accounting policies and accounting period of the Bank during the preparation of the consolidated financial statements, where the accounting policies and the accounting periods are inconsistent between the Bank and subsidiaries. For subsidiaries acquired in a business combination involving enterprises not under common control, the individual financial statements of the subsidiaries are adjusted based on the fair value of the identifiable assets and liabilities at the acquisition date.

All significant intra-group balances, transactions and unrealised profits are eliminated in the consolidated financial statements. The portion of equity and net profits or losses of a subsidiary not belonging to the Bank is recognised as minority interests and separately presented in equity and net profits respectively.

4.1.3 Functional currency

The functional currency of the group is Renminbi ("RMB").

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

#### 4.1.4 Foreign currency translation

Foreign currency transactions are translated into RMB using the exchange rates prevailing at the dates of the transactions.

At the balance sheet date, monetary items denominated in foreign currency are translated into RMB using the spot exchange rate on the balance sheet date. Exchange differences arising from these translations are recognised in profit or loss for the current period. Non-monetary items denominated in foreign currency that are measured in terms of historical cost are translated at the balance sheet date using the spot exchange rate at the date of the transaction.

#### 4.1.5 Cash and cash equivalents

The effect of exchange rate changes on cash is presented separately in the cash flow statement.

Cash and cash equivalents comprise cash in hand, deposits held at call with bank and short-term and highly liquid investments that are readily convertible to known amounts of cash and which are subject to an insignificant risk of changes in value.

#### 4.1.6 Financial assets

##### (a) Financial assets at fair value through profit or loss

These financial assets mainly include trading financial assets.

Financial assets are classified into the following categories at initial recognition: financial assets at fair value through profit or loss, loans and receivables, held-to-maturity investments and available-for-sale financial assets. The classification of financial assets depends on the Group's intention and ability to hold the financial assets.

If the financial asset being acquired or incurred principally for the purpose of selling or repurchasing in the near future, or forming a part of the portfolio of financial instruments that are managed together, and for which there is evidence of a recent actual pattern of short-term profit making, then it is classified in this category; derivatives are also classified as trading financial assets.

These assets are recognised at fair value upon purchase, and are measured at fair value at balance sheet date, gains and losses arising from changes in the fair value of these financial assets is included in the profit or loss account.

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

##### (b) Loans and receivables

Loans and receivables, including deposits with central bank, placement with and advances to banks and other financial institutions, financial assets purchased under resale agreements, loans and advances to customers and receivables, are non-derivative financial assets with fixed or determinable payments that are not quoted in an active market. They arise when the Group provides money, goods or services directly to a debtor with no intention of trading the receivable. Loans and receivables are initially recognised at the total of its fair value and transaction cost, and carried at amortised cost after the impairment loss discounted at the financial asset's original effective interest rate.

##### (c) Held-to-maturity investments

Held-to-maturity investments are non-derivative financial assets with fixed or determinable payments and fixed maturities that the Group's management has the positive intention and ability to hold to maturity. Held-to-maturity investments are initially recognised at the total of its fair value and transaction cost, and carried at amortised cost after the impairment loss discounted at the financial asset's original effective interest rate.

Other than in special circumstances (e.g. sale of an insignificant amount of held-to-maturity bonds at a time close to maturity), if the Group fails to hold them to maturity or reclassifies some to available-for-sale financial assets, the Group will reclassify the entire remaining bonds to available-for-sale financial assets, and change the measurement basis from amortised cost to fair value, and it will not be reclassified back to held-to-maturity investments in the current period and the following two full financial years.

##### (d) Available-for-sale financial assets

Available-for-sale financial assets are non-derivative financial assets that are either designated in this category at initial recognition or not classified as loan and receivables, held-to-maturity investments and financial assets at fair value through profit or loss. Available-for-sale financial assets are those intended to be held for an indefinite period of time, which may be sold in response to needs for liquidity or changes in interest rates, exchange rates and equity prices.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

Available-for-sale financial assets are initially recognised at fair value plus transaction costs upon acquisition and subsequently measured at fair value. At balance sheet date, gains and losses arising from changes in the fair value of available-for-sale financial assets are recognised net of tax directly in "Reserve from changes in fair value of available-for-sale financial assets" under shareholders' equity. When the financial asset is derecognised or impaired, the cumulative gain or loss previously recognised in equity is recognised in the income statement.

(e) Derecognition of financial assets

Financial assets are derecognised when one of the conditions below is met:

1) The rights to receive cash flows from the investments have expired; or

2) The Group has transferred substantially all risks and rewards relating to the ownership of the financial assets; or

3) The Group neither transfers nor retains substantially all the risks and rewards relating to the ownership of the financial asset, but has waived control over the financial assets.

When the financial assets are derecognised, the difference between the carryin amounts and amounts received plus the cumulative amounts of changes in fair value previously recognised in equity directly are recognised in profit or loss for the current period.

##### (f) Amortised cost

Amortised cost refers to the carrying amount of financial asset or liability at initial recognition less the paid principles, plus or minus the accumulative amount of amortisation incurred from amortising the difference between the initial recognised amount and the amount at maturity by using effective interest rate method, and less the impairment loss.

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

##### (g) Fair value

Fair value refers to the amount at which both knowledgeable parties, at their own free will, exchange their assets or clear off their debts under fair conditions. Regarding financial assets and financial liabilities, for which there is an active market, the Group uses the quotations in the active market to determine the fair value thereof. The quotations in the active market refer to the prices easily available from stock exchanges, brokers, industrial associations, pricing-service institutions, etc. and which represent the prices at which actually occurred market deals are made under fair conditions. If there is no active market for a financial asset, the Group establishes fair value using valuation techniques. Valuation techniques include using prices of recent market transactions between knowledgeable, willing parties, reference to the current fair value of another financial asset that is substantially the same as this instrument, and discounted cash flow analysis.

## 4.1.7 Offsetting financial assets and liabilities

Financial assets and financial liabilities are offset and the net amount is reported in the balance sheet when the Group has the legally enforceable right to set off the recognised amount and the transactions are intended to be settled on a net basis, and by realizing the asset and settling the liability simultaneously.

## 4.1.8 Impairment of financial assets

The Group assesses at each balance sheet date whether there is objective evidence that a financial asset or a group of financial assets excluding those fair valued through profit or loss is impaired. A financial asset or a group of financial assets is impaired and impairment losses are incurred only if there is objective evidence of impairment as a result of one or more events that occurred after the initial recognition of the asset and that loss event has an impact on the estimated future cash flows of the financial asset or group of financial assets that can be reliably estimated, the impairment loss is recognised in the income statement.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

Objective evidence that a financial asset or group of financial assets is impaired includes observable data that the borrower has severe financial difficulty, breach of contract or measurable decrease in the estimated future cash flows from a group of financial assets because of the change of economy conditions.

The Group first assesses whether objective evidence of impairment exists individually for financial assets that are individually significant. The Group performs a collective assessment for all other financial assets that are not individually significant or for which impairment has not yet been identified by including the asset in a group of financial assets with similar credit risk characteristics and collectively assesses them for impairment. Assets that are individually assessed for impairment and for which an impairment loss is or continues to be recognised are not included in a collective assessment of impairment.

##### (a) Assets carried at amortised cost

For the impaired loans and advances and held-to-maturity investments, the amount of the loss is measured as the difference between the asset's carrying amount and the present value of estimated future cash flows (excluding future credit losses that have not been incurred) discounted at the financial asset's original effective interest rate. The original effective interest rate is determined when the financial asset is initially recognised. With regard to floating rate loans, receivables and held-to-maturity investments, the discounted rate used for calculation of recoverable amount is the current effective interest rate as stipulated in the contract. In practice, the Group also applies market fair value of the financial assets to determine the losses. The estimated future cash flow excludes future credit losses that have not been incurred, but take into account the value of the collateral less costs for obtaining and selling the collateral.

Future cash flows in a group of financial assets that are collectively evaluated for impairment are estimated on the basis of the contractual cash flows of the assets in the group and historical loss experience for assets with credit risk characteristics similar to those in the group. Historical loss experience is adjusted on the basis of current observable data to reflect the effects of current conditions that did not affect the period on which the historical loss experience is based and to remove the effects of conditions in the historical period that do not currently exist.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

When a financial asset is uncollectible, it is written off against the related allowances for impairment after all the necessary procedures have been completed. Recoveries from the amounts previously written off were offset against impairment loss of the period.

If, in a subsequent period, the amount of the impairment loss decreases and the decrease can be related objectively to an event occurring after the impairment was recognised (such as an improvement in the debtor's credit rating), the previously recognised impairment loss is reversed by adjusting the allowance account and recognised in the income statement.

The Group performs individual impairment assessment on the assets classified under available-for-sale which are individually significant.

#### (b) Available-for-sale financial assets

When the available-for-sale financial assets are impaired, the cumulative loss – measured as the difference between the acquisition cost (net of any principal repayment and amortization) and current fair value, less any impairment loss on that financial asset previously recognised in profit or loss – previously recognised in capital reserve is removed from equity and recognised in the profit or loss for the current period.

Impairment losses recognised in the profit and loss account on equity instrument classified as available-for-sale financial asset are not reversed through the profit and loss account. If, in a subsequent period, the fair value of a debt instrument classified as available-for-sale financial asset increases and the increase can be objectively related to an event occurring after the impairment loss was recognised in profit or loss, the impairment loss is reversed through the profit and loss account.

## 4.1.9 Financial assets purchased under resale agreements and financial assets sold under repurchase agreements

Financial assets purchased under resale agreements are the agreements pursuant to which the Group purchases financial assets (including bonds and bills) at a certain price from the sellers who agree to buy back the securities on a specific future date at predetermined prices. Financial assets sold under repurchase agreements are the agreements pursuant to which the Group sells bonds, loans and bills at a certain price to the buyers who agree to sell back the financial assets on a specific future date at predetermined prices.

Financial assets purchased under resale agreements and financial assets sold under repurchase agreements are recognised at actual amounts paid at transaction dates and classified under the account caption of "financial assets purchased under resale agreements" and "financial assets sold under repurchase agreements" respectively. Bonds, loans and notes relating to "financial assets sold under repurchase agreements" are reflected in balance sheets.

## 4.1.10 Long-term equity investments

Long-term equity investments comprise the Bank's long-term equity investments in subsidiaries and the long-term equity investments where the Group has no control, joint control or significant influence over the investees, and which are not quoted in an active market and whose fair value cannot be reliably measured.

##### (a) Subsidiaries

Subsidiaries are all investees over which the Bank is able to control, i.e. has the power to govern the financial and operating policies so as to obtain benefits from their operating activities. The existence and effect of potential voting rights (including that derived from the convertible bonds and warrants that are currently convertible or exercisable) is considered to determine whether the Group has control over the investee. Investments in subsidiaries are measured using the cost method in the Bank's financial statements, and adjusted using the equity method when preparing the consolidated financial statements.

Long-term equity investments accounted for using the cost method are measured at the initial investments cost. Investments income is recognised in profit or loss for the cash dividends or profit declared by the investee.

(b) Other long-term equity investments

Other long-term equity investments where the Group does not have control, joint control or significant influence over the investee, and which are not quoted in an active market and whose fair value cannot be reliably measured are accounted for using the cost method.

## 4.1.11 Investment properties

Investment properties are rented the buildings held to generate rental income and is initially measured at cost. The subsequent cost occurred in association with investment properties is capitalised, if it is probable that the future economic benefit embodied with the item will flow to the Group and the cost of the item can be measured reliably, or expensed otherwise.

Investment properties are subsequently measured using cost method and are depreciated based on the estimated residual value ratios and the estimated useful life. The estimated useful life, residual value ratio and annual depreciation of the investment properties are as follow:

When the investment property has changed to self use purpose, the investment property will be treated as fixed or intangible asset from the date of the change. When the self used assets change for the purpose of generating rental income or earn capital gains, the fixed or intangible asset will be treated as investment property from the date of the change. When the change occurs, the carrying amount of the assets before the change will be recognised as the initial cost of assets after the change.

The estimated useful life of investment property, its estimated net residual value and depreciation method are reviewed and adjusted as appropriate annually at year end.

An investment property is derecognised on disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from its use or disposal. The amount of proceeds on sale, transfer, retirement or damage of an investment property net of its carrying amount and related taxes and expenses is recognised in the income statement for the current period.

4.1.12 Fixed assets

(a) Fixed assets recognition and initial measurement

Fixed assets comprise properties and buildings, machineries and equipment, transportation vehicles, computers and electronic equipment and office equipment. Properties and buildings mainly consist of branches' properties and office buildings.

Fixed assets are recognised when it is probable that the economic benefits associated with the assets will flow to the Group and its cost can be reliably measured. Constructed or purchased fixed assets are initially measured at cost at the time of acquisition.

Subsequent expenditures incurred for a fixed asset are included in the cost of the fixed asset when it is probable that the economic benefits associated with the fixed asset will flow to the Group and its cost can be reliably measured. The carrying amount of those parts that are replaced is derecognised and all the other subsequent expenditures are recognised in profit or loss in the period in which they are incurred.

#### (b) Fixed assets depreciation

Fixed assets are depreciated using the straight-line method to allocate the cost of the assets net of their estimated residual values over their estimated useful lives. For the fixed assets being provided for impairment loss, the related depreciation charge is prospectively determined based upon the adjusted carrying amounts over their remaining useful lives.

The estimated useful life, the estimated net residual value of a fixed asset and the depreciation method applied to the asset are reviewed, and adjusted as appropriate at each financial year-end.

##### (c) Disposal of fixed assets

A fixed asset is derecognised on disposal or when no future economic benefits are expected from its use or disposal. The amount of proceeds on sale, transfer, retirement or damage of a fixed asset net of its carrying amount and related taxes and expenses is recognised in profit or loss for the current period.

#### (d) Construction in progress

Construction in progress is measured at actual cost. Actual cost comprises construction costs, installation cost, borrowing costs that are eligible for capitalization and other costs necessary to bring the construction in progress ready for their intended use. Construction in progress is transferred to fixed assets when the assets are ready for their intended use, and depreciation begins from the following month.

## 4.1.13 Intangible assets

Intangible assets including land use rights and acquired computer softwares are measured at cost.

##### (a) Land use rights

Land use rights are amortised on the straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives from the year 2005 to 2074. If the purchased costs of land use rights and attached buildings cannot be reliably allocated between the land use rights and buildings, the purchase costs are recognised as fixed assets.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

##### (b) Computer software

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

Computer software are amortised on the straight-line basis over their estimated useful lives of five years since the inception of ready to use.

The estimated useful life of intangible assets and amortisation method are reviewed regularly and prospectively adjusted as appropriate.

## 4.1.14 Foreclosed assets

Foreclosed assets are initially recognised at fair value net of related expenses at the acquisition date, and subsequently measured at the lower of the book value and the fair value less cost to sell.

## 4.1.15 Impairment of non-financial assets

Fixed assets, construction in progress, investment properties measured using the cost model, intangible assets with definite useful life, long-term investments and other assets are tested for impairment if there is any indication that an asset may be impaired at the balance date. If the result of the impairment test indicates that the recoverable amount of the asset is less than its carrying amount, a provision for impairment and an impairment loss are recognised for the amount by which the asset's carrying amount exceeds its recoverable amount. The recoverable amount is the higher of an asset's fair value less costs to sell and the present value of the future cash flows expected to be derived from the asset. A provision for asset impairment is determined and recognised on an individual asset basis. If it is not possible to estimate the recoverable amount of an individual asset, the recoverable amount will be determined based on a group of assets to which the related asset belongs. A group of assets is the smallest group of assets which can independently generate cash inflows.

Once an impairment loss of these assets is recognised, it is not allowed to be reversed, even if the value of such asset is recovered in the subsequent periods.

4.1.16 Long-term prepaid expenses

Long-term prepaid expenses include the expenditure for improvements to fixed assets under operating lease and other prepayments incurred but should be borne by the current and subsequent periods and amortised over more than one year. Long-term prepaid expenses are amortised on the straight-line basis over the expected beneficial period and are presented at cost net of accumulated amortization.

## 4.1.17 Financial liabilities

Financial liabilities are classified into financial liabilities at fair value through profit or loss and other financial liabilities. The financial liabilities of the Group are mainly other liabilities, including placements from banks and other financial institutions, due to other banks and other financial institutions, financial assets sold under repurchase agreements, customer deposits, interests payables and other payables.

Other financial liabilities are measured initially at fair value and subsequently at amortized cost using effective interest method.

A financial liabilities may not be stopped from recognition, in all or in part, until the prevailing obligations of financial liabilities are all, or partly, dissolved. The difference between the carrying amounts of the financial liabilities stopped from recognition and the considerations paid shall be recognised in profit or loss.

## 4.1.18 Employee benefits

Employee benefits mainly include wages or salaries, bonuses, allowances and subsidies, staff welfare, social security contributions, housing funds, labour union funds, employee education funds and other expenditures incurred in exchange for service rendered by employees.

Employee benefits are recognised as a liability in the accounting period in which an employee has rendered service, and as costs of assets or expenses to whichever the employee service is attributable except for the compensation payments for labor dismissed.

The Group participates in employee social security plans, including pension, medical, housing and other social welfare benefits, organized and managed by the government authorities, whose costs are charged to the income statement immediately when they occur. In addition to these plans, employees can also voluntarily participate in a defined contribution annuity plan established by the Group. The Group contributes to the annuity plan based on certain percentages of the employees' gross salaries.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

The Group has also provided supplemental retirement benefits and early retirement benefits to retired employees and those employees who accepted an early retirement arrangement. Supplemental retirement benefits include supplemental pension payments and medical expense coverage. Early retirement benefits have been paid to those employees who accept voluntary retirement before the normal retirement date, as approved by management. The related benefit payments are made from the date of early retirement to the normal retirement date. The above supplemental retirement benefits and early retirement benefits obligation are recorded on the accrual basis.

## 4.1.19 Deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities

Deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are calculated and recognised based on the differences arising between the tax base of assets and liabilities and their carrying amount (temporary differences). The deductible losses that can be carried forward to deduct the taxable profit in subsequent years in accordance with the tax law are regarded as the temporary difference and for which a deferred tax asset is recognised. No deferred tax asset or deferred tax liability is recognised for the temporary differences resulting from the initial recognition of an asset or liability due to transaction other than a business combination which affects neither accounting profit nor taxable profit (or deductible loss). At the balance sheet date, deferred tax assets and deferred tax liabilities are measured at the tax rates that are expected to apply to the period when the asset is realised or the liability is settled.

Deferred tax assets are only recognised for deductible temporary differences, deductible losses and tax credits to the extent that it is probable that taxable profit will be available in the future against which the deductible temporary differences, deductible losses and tax credits can be utilised.

Deferred tax liabilities are recognised for temporary differences arising from investments in subsidiaries, except where the Bank is able to control the timing of the reversal of the temporary difference, and it is probable that the temporary difference will not reverse in the foreseeable future. When it is probable that the temporary differences arising from investments in subsidiaries will be reversed in the foreseeable future and that the taxable profit will be available in the future against which the temporary differences can be utilised, the corresponding deferred tax assets are recognised.
