#### 4.1.20 Profit distribution

Proposed profit distribution is recognised as a liability in the period in which it is approved by the shareholders' meeting.

## 4.1.21 Provision

Provisions for providing guarantee services, pending litigation or arbitrations and onerous contracts are recognised when the Group has a present obligation, and it is probable that an outflow of economic benefits will be required to settle the obligation, and the amount of the obligation can be measured reliably.

A provision is initially measured at the best estimate of the expenditure required to settle the related present obligation. Factors surrounding a contingency such as the risks, uncertainties and the time value of money are taken into account as a whole in reaching the best estimate of a provision. Where the effect of the time value of money is material, the best estimate is determined by discounting the related future cash outflows. The increase in the discounted amount of the provision arising from passage of time is recognised as interest expense. The carrying amount of provisions is reviewed at each balance sheet date and adjusted as appropriate to reflect the current best estimate.

#### 4.1.22 Interest incomes and expense

Interest income and expense are recognised in the profit and loss account for financial instruments carried at amortised cost and available-for-sale interest-bearing instruments, on an accrual basis using the effective interest method.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

The effective interest method is a method of calculating the amortised cost of a financial asset or a financial liability and allocating the interest income or interest expense over the relevant period. The effective interest rate is the rate that exactly discounts estimated future cash payments or receipts through the expected life of the financial instrument or, when appropriate, a shorter period to the net carrying amount of the financial asset or financial liability. When calculating the effective interest rate, the Group estimates cash flows considering all contractual terms of the financial instrument but does not consider future credit losses. The calculation includes all fees and points paid or received between contract parties, transaction costs and all other premiums or discounts directly related to the contracts that are an integral part of the effective interest rate.

Once financial assets have been written down as a result of an impairment loss, interest income is recognised using the rate of interest used to discount the future cash flows for the purpose of measuring the impairment loss.

#### 4.1.23 Fee and commission incomes and expenses

Fees and commission are normally recognised under accrual basis at the time of rendering services.

#### 4.1.24 Lease

A finance lease is a lease that transfers substantially all the risks and rewards incidental to ownership of an asset. An operating lease is a lease other than a finance lease.

Payments made under operating leases are expensed in the income statement on a straight-line basis over the period of the lease.

#### 4.1.25 Contingent liabilities

A contingent liability is a possible obligation that arises from past events and whose existence will only be confirmed by the occurrence or non-occurrence of one or more uncertain future events not wholly within the control of the Group. It can also be a present obligation arising from past events that is not recognised because it is not probable that an outflow of economic benefits will be required or the amount of obligation cannot be measured reliably.

Contingencies are disclosed in the notes of financial statements, and only be recognised when it is probable that an outflow of economic benefits will be required and the amount of obligation can be measured reliably.

#### 4.1.26 Acceptance

Acceptance is the guarantee provided by the Bank on the bills issued by customers. The Bank expects that most of the bills acceptance will be fulfilled and settled by the customers at the same time. Acceptance is accounted for as an off-balance sheet item and disclosed in Note 8.1.

#### 4.1.27 Guarantee contracts

Guarantee contracts issued by the Bank include letters of guarantee and letters of credit. Through such guaranteed contracts, the Bank makes advance payment upon guarantors' failure to honor their commitment in the contracts.

The Bank initially recognises the guarantee contracts at fair value and amortises at a certain rate during the guaranteed period. Subsequently, they are carried at the higher of amortised carrying value or the provision required to meet the Bank's guarantee obligation. The changes in carrying value are recorded in the income statement.

The guaranteed amounts of guarantee contracts are disclosed as off-balance sheet item in note 8.1.

#### 4.1.28 Fiduciary activities

The Group commonly acts as a trustee that results in its holding or managing assets on behalf of individuals, trusts and other institutions. These assets and profit or loss arising thereon are excluded from the financial statements, as they are not the assets of the Group.

The Group provides custody and trustee services to customers (as the entrustor) who provide funds and bear the risks. According to the objective, purpose of use, amounts, terms and interest rates decided by the principal, the Group (as the entrustee) acts as an agent in lending, supervising and collecting the loans while the principal bears the risks. The Group does not make advance or bear credit risk and thus the entrusted loans are recorded off-balance sheet. The Group only charges commission, which is recognised as income according to the revenue recognition policy on the accrual basis.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

#### 4.1.29 Segment information

The Group identifies operating segments based on the internal organisation structure, management requirements and the internal reporting system, and discloses segment information of reportable segments determined on the basis of operating segments.

An operating segment is a component of the Group that satisfies all of the following conditions: (1) the component is able to earn revenues and incur expenses from ordinary activities; (2) whose operating results are regularly reviewed by the Group's management to make decisions about resources to be allocated to the segment and to assess its performance, and (3) for which the information on financial position, operating results and cash flows is available to the Group. If two or more operating segments have similar economic characteristics, and satisfy certain conditions, they are aggregated into a single operating segment.

The management does not disclose segment information for fiscal year 2010, based on the fact that the Group's assets and clients are mainly in Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region, the management of the Group is of the view that there is no need to prepare segment information for the year 2010.

# 4.2 Critical accounting estimates and judgments

The Group makes estimates and assumptions that affect the reported amounts of assets and liabilities within the next financial year. Estimates and judgements are continually evaluated and are based on historical experience and other factors, including expectations of future events that are believed to be reasonable under the circumstances. Areas susceptible to changes in essential estimates and judgements, which affect the carrying value of assets and liabilities, are set out below. It is impracticable to determine the effect of changes to either the key assumptions discussed below or other estimation uncertainties. It is possible that actual results may require material adjustments to the estimates referred to below.

# 1. Impairment allowances on loans and receivables

The Group reviews its loan portfolios to assess impairment regularly, and would further assess impairment loss when there are indications of impairment. Objective evidence of impairment includes observable data indicating that there is a measurable decrease in the estimated future cash flows from an individual loan, observable data indicating that there has been an adverse change in the payment status of borrowers in a group (e.g. payment delinquency or default), or national or local economic conditions that correlated with defaults on assets in the group. The impairment loss amount for the loans under individual assessment is the net decrease of loans expected future cash flow. When assessing the impairment loss of a loan portfolio under the collective evaluation method, management uses estimates based on historical loss experience, which subjects to adjustments according to observable data to reflect the current economic conditions, for assets with credit risk characteristics and objective evidence of impairment similar to those in the portfolio when estimating expected future cash flows. The methodology and assumptions used for estimating both the amount and timing of future cash flows are reviewed regularly to reduce any differences between loss estimates and actual loss experience.

# 2. Income taxes

There are certain transactions and calculations for which the ultimate tax determination is uncertain during the ordinary course of business. Significant estimates are required in determining the provision for income taxes. The Group recognises tax liabilities for anticipated tax audit issues based on estimates of whether additional taxes will be due. Where the final tax outcome of these matters is different from the amounts that were initially recorded, such differences will impact the income tax and deferred tax provisions in the period during which such a determination is made. Management believes that it is probable that taxable profit will be available in the future against which the deductible temporary differences can be utilised.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

# 3. Fair value of financial instruments

The Group establishes fair value of financial instruments where there is no active market by using valuation techniques. The valuation techniques include models such as discounted cash flow analysis using risk-adjusted interest rates. In practice, these models use observable market inputs and data whenever possible, but management still have to evaluate the assumption of counterparty creditworthiness, market volatilities and other relevant factors. The fair value assessment of the financial instruments will be affected if the assumptions above have changed.

# 4. Held-to-maturity investments

The Group classifies non-derivative financial assets with fixed or determinable payments and fixed maturity as held-to-maturity. This classification requires significant judgment. In making this judgment, the Group evaluates its intention and ability to hold such investments to maturity. If the Group sell significant amount of held-to-maturity assets before the maturity date, the entire category would be reclassified as available-for-sale investments, and measured at fair value instead of amortised cost.

# 5 TAXATION

# 5.1 Corporate income tax

The Group is subject to the "Corporate Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China" (the "new CIT Law"), approved by the National People's Congress on 16 March 2008. According to new CIT law, the corporate income tax rate applicable to the Group is 25% (2009: 25%).

# 5.2 Business tax

Pursuant to tax regulations, except for the interest income from inter-bank and intra-bank transactions, interest income from government bonds which are exempted for business tax, operating business income of the Group is subject to business tax at the basis of 5% of the revenue.

# 5.3 City construction and maintenance tax

The tax basis for city construction and maintenance tax is 7% of the business tax.

# 5.4 Educational surcharges

The tax basis for educational surcharges is 3% of business tax, and 1% of business tax for local educational surcharges.

(a) On 11 July 2008, the Bank issued 1,770,345,000 shares to 17 designated shareholders including Nanning New Technology Industry Construction and Development Company (the "17 Investors") with the par value of RMB 1 each and increased share capital by RMB 1,770,345,000. The capital has been injected into the Bank and recorded as share capital.

In 2008, the resolution was passed by extraordinary shareholders' meeting that the shareholders of the Bank agreed to treat the recovered amounts from non-performing assets, which are originally attributable to the 17 investors, as share premium of new shares directionally issued above, and to record as capital reserve – share premium. The number of shares held by the 17 investors remained unchanged.

In 2008, the Bank received the net recovered amount from non-performing assets sold to 17 Investors of RMB317,687,404. In 2009, the Bank received the net recovered amount from non-performing assets sold to 17 Investors of RMB496,862,967. In the current year, the Bank received the net recovered amount from non-performing assets sold to 17 Investors of RMB557,960,567. This amount was recorded as share premium.

<table border=1 style='margin: auto; word-wrap: break-word;'><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'></td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>31 December 2010 Group &amp; Bank</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>31 December 2009 Group &amp; Bank</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>As at 1 January</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>146,697,765</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>80,856,965</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>Current year additions (a)</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>77,839,100</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>65,840,800</td></tr><tr><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>As at 31 December</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>224,536,865</td><td style='text-align: center; word-wrap: break-word;'>146,697,765</td></tr></table>

Pursuant to regulations issued by Ministry of Finance, the Bank is required to establish and maintain a general risk reserve within owners' equity, through the appropriation of income to address unidentified potential impairment losses. In general, the general reserve should not be less than 1% of the aggregate amount of risk assets at period end. The appropriation of general risk reserve should be treated as distribution and as part of owner's equity.

(a) Pursuant to a resolution approved in the general meeting held on 23 April 2010, the Bank appropriated RMB77,839,100 from the net profit for the year 2010 to the general risk reserve (2009: RMB65,840,800).

## 6.1 Dividends

As stated in Note 6.22, according to the resolution approved in the shareholder's meeting on 23 April 2010, the Bank distributed a cash dividend of RMB 0.3 (tax included) per 10 shares with an aggregate amount of RMB 60,000,000, which was calculated based on the total shares (2,000,000,000 shares) after capital injection in 2008.

## 7 RELATED PARTY TRANSACTIONS

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

### 7.1 Related parties relationships

Related parties of the Group refer to entities controlled or jointly controlled by or under significant influence of the Group; entities that control, jointly control or have significant influence over the Group; or entities with which the Group is under control, joint control or significant influence of another party. Related parties can be individuals or enterprises. Related parties that have significant influence on the Group include: the director, companies controlled or significantly influenced by members of the Board of Directors and the Board of Supervisors, senior management or their related persons, the subsidiaries of these companies, and major shareholders with the power to influence the operating decision-making or financial policies of the Group.

Shareholders who owned 5% or more of equity interests of the Bank include: Guangxi Ronggui Trading Company, Guangxi Liuzhou Iron & Steel Group Company, Guangxi Guiguan Electric Power Co., Ltd, Giant Investment Co., Ltd, Oceanwide Construction Group Co., Ltd, Guangxi Ronghe Corporation Group Co., Ltd and Liuzhou Liangmianzhen Co., Ltd (Note 6.24).

(a) The basic information of the Bank's subsidiary is set out in Note 6.9(a).

## 12 FINANCIAL RISK MANAGEMENT

### 12.1 Overview

The Group's activities expose it to a variety of financial risks and those activities involve the analysis, evaluation, acceptance and management of various degree of risk or combination of risks. Taking risk is core to financial business, and the operational risks are an inevitable consequence of being in business. The Group's aim is therefore to maximize value for shareholders while maintaining risk within acceptable parameters and satisfying the requirements of the regulatory authorities, depositors and other interest groups for the Group's prudent and stable development.

The Group's risk management policies are designed to identify and analyse these risks, to set appropriate risk limits and controls, and to monitor the risk and adherence to limits by means of reliable information system.

The Board of Directors of the Group is responsible for approving risk management strategies, procedures, principles and policies. The senior management of the Group manages the Group-wide risks as well as risks arising from specific business under the approved risk management principles and policies. In addition, internal audit is responsible for the independent review of the execution of policies, the reporting and recommendation made to the Board of Directors and the communication with corresponding risk management units. The most significant types of financial risks to the Group are credit risk, market risk and liquidity risk. Market risk includes currency risk and interest rate risk.

### 12.2 Credit risk

Credit risk is the risk that a customer or counterparty will cause a financial loss for the Group by failing or unwilling to discharge an obligation. Change of economy condition or deterioration in the quality of credit assets of certain industries could potentially cause financial losses. Balance sheet credit exposures arise from lending activities such as loans and advances, debt securities investments and transaction with other banks. There is also credit risk in off-balance sheet financial instruments, such as off-balance sheet commitments. The business is conducted in Guangxi, which results in the concentration risk because the loan portfolio of the Group is more prone to be affected by the region's economic conditions changes. Therefore, the Group manages the credit exposure prudently. The risk management department at headquarter is responsible for the management of overall credit risk (including loans, debt securities investments and transaction with other banks), and reporting to senior management periodically. The Group has set up appropriate functions and set risk limits for specific individuals. The risk limits are monitored and reviewed at least annually.

#### 12.2.1 Credit risk measurement

According to "Guiding Principles on the Risk-based Classification of Loans", the five categories are defined as follows:

Pass: borrowers can honour the terms of the contracts, and there is no reason to doubt their ability to repay principal and interest of loans in full and on a timely basis.

The Group measures and manages the credit quality of loans and advances to corporate and personal customers based on the "Guiding Principles on the Risk-based Classification of Loans" issued by the CBRC, which requires Chinese commercial banks to classify their corporate and personal loans into five categories: pass, special mention, substandard, doubtful and loss, among which loans the last three categories are regarded as non-performing loans.

(i) Loans and advances and off-balance sheet commitments

Special mention: borrowers are still able to service the loans currently, although the repayment of loans might be adversely affected by some factors.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

Substandard: borrowers' ability to service loans is apparently in question, cannot depend on their normal business revenues to repay the principal and interest of loans and certain losses might be incurred even with the enforcement of the guarantees.

Doubtful: borrowers cannot repay principal and interest of loans in full and significant losses will be incurred even with the enforcement of the guarantees. Loss: principal and interest of loans cannot be recovered or only a small portion can be recovered after taking all possible measures and resorting to necessary legal procedures.

(ii) Placements with banks and other financial institutions

The Group sets credit limit or implement acceptance controls in granting credit to other banks and adopts risk management policies similar to corporate customers for those non-bank financial institutions.

#### 12.2.3 Credit limit management and mitigation policies

In order to manage concentrations of credit risk, the Group has adopted credit limit controls including specifying the limit of risk exposure accepted to one borrower, industry segments, one financial institute counterparty and to related parties.

Other management and mitigation policies include:

#### (i) Collateral

The Group employs a range of policies and practices to mitigate credit risk. The most typical of these is the taking of security for funds advances (collateral), margin deposit, corporate or personal guarantees, which is common practice. The principal types of collateral for corporate loans and advances are:

- Financial products: such as bank deposit, public traded stocks, bonds or bills, insurance contracts and gold.

• Physicals: such as real estates (including residential, shops, offices, and factories), machineries, ships and aircrafts.

## 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

The Group appoints professional valuation agencies to evaluate the collateral. In order to mitigate the credit risk, the Group has set the maximum collateral rates (i.e. the ratios of loan amount over fair value of collateral) for different types of collateral. For loans guaranteed by a third party guarantor, the Group will assess the guarantor's credit rating, financial condition, credit history and the ability to discharge obligations.

##### (ii) Credit commitments

The main purpose of credit commitment is to make sure the customers could obtain the required fund when necessary. Letter of guarantee is an irrevocable commitment provided by the Group with the obligations to pay for the customers when they are unable to fulfill the liabilities to the third-party. The commitment bears the credit risk similar to loans. The Group obtains margin deposits to mitigate the credit risk exposure when the applied amount for credit commitment exceeds the approved credit limit. The potential credit risk exposure faced by the Group equal to total amount of credit commitment.

##### (iii) Loan commitments

Loan commitment represents the unused portion of loan facilities granted to customers. The execution of most loan commitment is contingent upon customers maintaining specific credit standards, the compliance of the loan project and risk benefit radio. The likely credit risk loss amount that the Group is exposed to is less than total unused loan commitments. The Group monitors the term to maturity of loan commitments because longer-term commitments generally have a greater degree of credit risk than shorter-term commitments.

#### 12.2.3 Impairment and provisioning policy

In accordance with the accounting policies, if there is any objective evidence that the estimated future cash flows generated from the financial assets decrease and the amount can be reliably estimated, the Group considers the financial assets are impaired and makes an impairment provision.

The criteria set out by the Group to determine whether objective evidences of impairment exist include:

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

- The borrower's operation has been ceased or nearly ceased;

- The borrower obtained the loans through willful misconduct or fraudulent behaviors and try not to fulfill the obligation;

- The Group has taken legal procedures to collect the loan;

As for project loans, the major construction project has been ceased;

- The repayment relies on income from sale of manufacturing or operational fixed assets, collateral or repayment from the guarantor;

3orrower has negative net assets;

- A default or delinquency in interest or principal payment:

- The loan has been past due and cannot be repaid by the borrower's own business;

- The source of repayment mainly depends on the value of the collateral but its value has been decreased significantly;

- The source of repayment is primarily guarantor's financial support but the guarantor is in a weak financial condition as well;

Restructured loan:

- The borrower borrows new loans to repay the old ones for several times, and the borrower has no sufficient cash to repay the loans;

- Continuous deterioration of the financial condition of the borrower;

Other evidence indicates the potential impairment

The Group performs the review of individual significant financial assets at least quarterly. Impairment allowances on individually assessed accounts are determined by an evaluation of the incurred loss at balance-sheet date on a case-by-case basis using discounted cash flow analysis. The assessment normally encompasses collateral held (including reconfirmation of its enforceability) and the anticipated receipts for that individual account.

Impairment and provisioning policy(continued)

(a) Loans and advances neither past due nor impaired

The credit risk of neither past due nor impaired loans can be accessed by reference to the CBRC's loan five-classification system adopted by the Group.

(b) Loans past due but not impaired

Loans and advances less than 90 days past due are not considered impaired, unless other information is available to indicate the contrary.

An analysis of loans past due but not impaired by past due days is as follows:

Prior to loan disbursement, the Group appointed valuation agencies to evaluate the collateral and pledges. The Group performs valuation of the collateral to reassess whether the collateral could cover the credit risk exposure in case the significant deterioration in value of the collateral's occurs.

As at 31 December 2010, the fair value of collateral held for impaired corporate loans amounted to RMB 231,378,046 (2009:RMB 157,419,829), the fair value of collateral held for impaired retail loans amounted to RMB 53,247,890 (2009:RMB 58,680,834).

After performed individual assessments on the above corporate loans and taken fully consideration of the realizable value of the collateral, the group made provision of RMB 70,099,009 and also the bank made provision of RMB 69,928,148 (2009: RMB 100,452,625)(Note 6.6).

The majority of personal loans are individual business loans and residential mortgage loans. The Group strictly follows related regulation issued by PBOC and CBRC according to which the mortgage rate of residential mortgage loans is normally no higher than 70% so as to ensure the sufficiency of collateral. The Group implements loan five-classification system for personal loans, which collectively take account of mortgage coverage rate, overdue days, repayment ability and repayment willingness, etc, through which the Group is able to take appropriate measures earlier to reduce loss by doing loan classification properly.

The Group and the Bank performed individual assessments on the above impaired personal loan and made a provision of RMB 8,342,400 (2009:RMB 17,653,060)(Note 6.6).

##### (d) Rescheduled loans and advances

Rescheduled loans refer to the loans the credit terms of which have been rescheduled as a result of the deterioration in the borrower's financial condition or of the borrower's inability to make payments when due. Prior to approving the rescheduling of the loans, the Group typically requires additional guarantees, pledges and/or collateral, or the assumption of the loan by a borrower with better repayment ability.

As at 31 December 2010, the rescheduled loans of the Group is 49,992,083 (2009: Nil)

#### 12.2.4 Credit assets

As stated in Note 6.8, the Group invested in credit assets related to trust products in fiscal year 2010 which are issued by other financial institutions. The management believes that credit risk is small, since the counterparties are with good credit ratings and the investments are all due within one year.

# 12.3 Market risk

Market risk is due to the adverse movement to the exposure of interest rate products, equities and commodities, which are caused by general or special changes in interest rates, exchange rates, commodity price and equity prices. The market risk the Group faces mainly arises from the interest rate risk.

The risk management is aimed to enhance the shareholder value as well as control the risk to a tolerable level. The Group's market risk management framework comprises three layers. The Board of Directors and the risk management committee is the ultimate decision making function. The operational management and its risk management execution committee is responsible for the design of risk management policies and procedures, implement policy and monitor, risk control and compliance operation. The risk management department is responsible for monitoring the overall market risk of the trading account and the banking account, and ensure overall and individual market risk are controlled within a tolerable level.

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

## 12.3.1 Market risks measurement techniques

The Group's foreign currency business is not significant and thus the Group's primary market risk is the interest rate risk. The Group has designed the market risk management policy according to the "Commercial Bank Market Risk Management Guidance" issued by CBRC. The Group manages the interest rate risk primarily through interest rate sensitivity gap analysis. Following market risk management framework, the Group has established risk limit controls on the limit for different products and total market risks, and established risk monitoring reporting system to report to management and the board regularly.

## 12.3.2 Interest rate risk

The Group formulates interest risk management policy and adopts the proper framework and methods to identify, measure, monitor and control the interest rate risk.

The Board of Directors and its risk management committee are responsible for the management of the Group's interest rate risk. The risk management committee is responsible for the monitoring of the interest rate risk management. The treasury department manages the interest rate risk according to the relevant policies, and closely supervises the related risks and reports to the Board of Directors and risk management committee on a regularly basis. The Group will improve the management system of the interest rate risk and gradually realise the integrated management of market risk.

##### The interest risk of the Group is mainly structural risk which includes:

Interest sensitivity gap risk: Interest rate risk arises mainly from mismatches in the maturities, re-pricing periods or benchmark interest rates of assets and liabilities;

Yield curve risk: The yield curves shift up or down in non-parallel, resulting in the curves being more steeper or flatter, and the negative impact on interest income or economic value;

Benchmark interest rates risk: Different pricing benchmark for different transactions may lead to return rate of assets and cost of liabilities fluctuating differently during the same repricing period.

GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

Interest margins may increase as a result of fluctuation in market interest rates, but may reduce or create losses in the event that unexpected movements arise. Currently, benchmark interest rates for RMB loans and deposits in the PRC are set by PBOC and the Group's domestic business is subject to the interest rate scheme regulated by the PBOC. It is normal practice for the interest rates of both interest-bearing assets and liabilities to move in tandem, although the timing an extent of such movements may not be synchronized. This significantly mitigates the exposure of the Group to RMB interest rate risk. However, there is no guarantee that the PBOC will continue this practice in future.

The Group manages the interest rate risk in the banking book primarily through interest rate repricing gap analysis. Interest rate repricing gap analysis measures the difference between the amount of interest-bearing assets and interest-bearing liabilities that mature or must be repriced within certain periods and is used to generate indicators of interest rate sensitivity of earnings and economic value to changing interest rates.

When performing the interest rate sensitivity analysis, the Group makes the following assumptions in determining the business conditions and financial parameters:

a. Not take into account the changes of business subsequent to the balance sheet date; the analysis is based on the static gap as at the balance sheet date;

b. The interest rates of different interest-bearing assets and different interest-bearing assets liabilities vary to the same extent;

c. All repriced assets and liabilities are repriced at the middle point of the relevant period;

d. Not take into account the effect of interest rate changes on customer behavior:

e. Not take into account the effect of interest rate changes on market price

f. Not take into account the effect of interest rate changes on off-balance sheet products;

g. Not take into account the actions that would be taken by the Group to mitigate the impact caused by interest rate changes.

Due to the above restrictive conditions, it is likely the actual change of net interest income caused by the changes of interest rates is different from the result of sensitivity analysis.

## 12.4 Liquidity risk

Liquidity risk is the risk that the Group is unable to obtain funds at a reasonable cost when required to meet a repayment obligation and fund its asset portfolio within a certain time.

The Group's liquidity risk management framework comprises three layers. The Board of Directors including the risk management committee is the ultimate decision making body. The assets and liability management committee and risk management execution committee are responsible for the designing and monitoring of risk management measures and mechanism. The daily liquidity management is led by treasury department, and supported by finance and other department, which are responsible for monitoring of liquidity risk and regular reporting to the management and local supervisory authorities.

According to the PBOC regulations, the ratio of loan to deposit could not exceed 75%.

As of 31 December 2010, 16.5% of the Bank's total RMB denominated deposits must be deposited with PBOC as statutory deposit reserve (2009: 13.5%), while 12.5% of the subsidiary's total RMB denominated deposits must be deposited with PBOC as statutory deposit reserve.

The matching and controlled mismatching of the maturities and interest rates of assets and liabilities is fundamental to the management of the Group. It is unusual for banks to be completely matched, as transacted business is often of uncertain term and of different types. An unmatched position potentially enhances profitability, but also increases the risk of losses.

The matching of maturities of assets and liabilities and the ability to replace, at an acceptable cost, the interest-bearing liabilities as they mature are important factors in assessing the liquidity of the Group and its exposure to changes in interest rates and exchange rates.

The Group offers guarantee and issues letter of credit based on the creditability of customers and margin deposits placed by the customers. Normally the customers will not draw down the full amount of guarantee provided by the Group, thus the required cash to cover the guarantee provided by the Group is less than the committed amount. At the same time, many of the credit commitments are expired or terminated and are not actually executed, thus the credit commitments do not represent the total demand of the fund in the future.

## 12.5 Fair Value

(a) Financial instruments not measured at fair value

Financial assets and liabilities not measured at fair value mainly include cash and deposits with central bank, due from other banks, financial assets purchased under resale agreements, interest receivables, loans and advances to customers, held-to-maturity investments, other financial assets, due to other banks and other financial institutions, placements from other banks and other financial institutions, financial assets sold under repurchase agreements, customers deposits and interest payables, other financial liabilities.

The fair value of loans and advances to customers are measured with cashflow of principals and interests discounted using RMB benchmark loan rates published by PBOC. The fair value of customers deposits are measured with cashflow of principals and interests discounted using RMB benchmark loan rates published by PBOC.

For financial assets not measured at fair value, such as cash and deposits with central bank, and due from other banks, their carrying amount equals their fair value since they mature within one year. For financial liabilities not measured at fair value, such as due to other banks and other financial institutions, placements from other banks and other financial institutions, their carrying amount equals their fair value since they mature within one year.

(b) Financial instruments measured at fair value

Based on the lowest level input that is significant to the fair value measurement in its entirety, the fair value hierarchy has the following levels:

Level 1: Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities.

Level 3: Inputs for the asset or liability that are not based on observable market data (that is, unobservable inputs)

Level 2: Inputs other than quoted prices included within level 1 that are observable for the asset or liability, either directly (that is, as prices) or indirectly (that is, derived from prices).

The fair value of a financial instrument that is traded in an active market is determined at the quoted price in the active market. The fair value of a financial instrument that is not traded in an active market is determined by using a valuation technique. Valuation techniques include using prices of recent market transactions between knowledgeable and willing parties, reference to the current fair value of another financial asset that is substantially the same with this instrument, and discounted cash flow analysis. Inputs to valuation techniques include prepayment rates, rates of estimated credit losses, and interest rates or discount rates.

Available-for-sale equity instruments are equity investments in Bank of Communications and in Guanglian (Nanning) Investment Company. As Ganglian (Nanning) Investment Company is a non-public company with no records for its initial shares historical transactions, the fair value is not available. Therefore, the equity investments of the Group in Guanglian (Nanning) Investment Company are listed in Level 3.

There are no changes in level 3 financial assets for the year 2009 and 2010.

As at 31 December 2010, gain recognised in profit or loss for fiscal year 2010 is 0 for level 3 financial assets held by the group;

As at 31 December 2009, gain recognised in profit or loss for fiscal year 2009 is 0 for level 3 financial assets held by the group.

## 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

##### GUANGXI BEIBU GULF BANK CO., LTD

NOTES TO THE FINANCIAL STATEMENTS FOR THE YEAR ENDED 31 DECEMBER 2010 (All amounts in RMB unless otherwise stated) [English Translation for Reference Only]

## 12.6 Capital management

The Group's capital management focus on capital adequacy ratios and return on capital ratio, the Group's objectives when managing capital are to support the Group's development plan, to achieve the Group's growth and profitability, to optimise the assets scale and structure and to optimise the capital scale and capital return.

The Group sets the target range of capital adequacy ratios by taking account of regulatory ratios, industry average level, and its own growth rate, time frame of capital adequacy and stability of equity return. The target range of capital adequacy ratios should not be less than the regulatory ratios. The Group calculates capital adequacy ratios in accordance with "Administration Measures Concerning Capital Adequacy Ratios of Commercial Groups" issued by CBRC and other regulations.

#### The Board of Directors, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd. Annual Report 2010

##### For the attention of all shareholders:

In 2010, the financial situation at home and abroad is complex. Horizontal competition is increasingly fierce while monetary and credit policy is gradually tightening. In such a tough environment, the Board of Directors of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank has fully discharged their decision-making functions, leading employees of the bank in continuing to meet the difficulties and in promotion of a pioneering spirit, withstanding pressure, overcoming difficulties, and have achieved good results in all of their work. On behalf of the Board of Directors of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Corporation, I now make the annual working report to the General Meeting of Shareholders for 2010, for your consideration.

# 1. Strengthening research and judgment of the economic and financial situation and offering decision guidance on the operation and management

In 2010, the international and domestic economic and financial situation is very severe and complex, full of many challenges for Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank's decision-makers. The China Banking Regulatory Commission is strict regarding the size, structure and delivery schedule of bank loans, creating enormous pressure for business development and operations. A growing number of joint-stock commercial banks and commercial banks from other cities have entered Guangxi, bringing white-hot competition to the market sector. To this end, the Board of Directors have strengthened their analysis and judgment capabilities in response to the economic and financial situation, paying special attention to providing more forward-looking guidance on the business activities of business management. In 2010, the Board of Directors issued the Guidance of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Risk Management for 2010, Analysis of the Economic and Financial Situation in the Second Half of 2010 and other guidance materials, also conducting analysis and discussion of the business strategy of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank under the current economic and financial situation at the quarterly meeting of the Board of Directors, playing an important guiding role for the businesses of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in 2010.

## 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

## II. Strengthening efforts in urging the operation management to complete the annual business for 2010

At the end of 2009, the Board of Directors strengthened the management and supervision of business management activities by issuing the System of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Information Reporting of Business Management (Trial) and the System of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Implementation of Resolutions of General Meeting of Shareholders, Board of Directors, and Special Committees Thereunder (Trial). In 2010 the two systems were fully implemented, greatly enhancing the supervision and management power of the Board of Directors. Under the powerful direction of the Board of Directors, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank strengthened basic management and risk management, vigorously expanded business, steadily promoted various operational and management works, and withstood the severe test of the international and domestic financial environments, exceeding the business task of the Board of Directors, and achieving encouraging results in operations.

(i) Overall operation in the year was sound: operating efficiency increased throughout the year and profitability continued to improve; the asset business grew rapidly; debt business grew rapidly and the debt portfolio was diversified; efficiency in the use of capital steadily increased and the return to shareholders increased; the bank has steadily developed and expanded the intermediate business, intermediate business products are becoming more valuable year on year, also anti-risk capabilities were further enhanced. As of December 31, 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank's total assets reached 59.035 billion yuan, 6.4 times of that before the reform and restructuring, with an increase of 31.836 billion yuan over 2009, up by 117.05%; the deposit balance was 34.156 billion yuan, 3.9 times of that before the reform and restructuring, with an increase of 10.733 billion yuan over 2009, up by 45.8% which was 22.06 percentage points higher than the average increase; loan balance was 17.205 billion yuan, 4.1 times of that before the reform and restructuring, with an increase of 3.87 billion yuan over 2009, up by 29.03%; operating income was 1.21 billion yuan, with an increase of 439 million yuan over the previous year, up by 56.84%; and profit after provisions was 587 million yuan, with an increase of 322 million yuan, up by 122%.

(II) Major breakthroughs were achieved in the main works, showing five exciting highlights.

1. Strategic positioning was further clarified and the capacity of serving SMEs was significantly improved. In the face of multiple challenges such as the complex and changing international financial situation and with monetary and credit policy controls in 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank considered the situation and overcame the difficulties, clarified strategic positioning, and steadily increased its efforts in support of SMEs. As of December 31, 2010, the balance of loans was 17.205 billion yuan, including 9.867 billion yuan to support construction of SMEs, accounting for 57.35% of total bank loans, greatly supporting the construction and development of SMEs in the region and effectively promoting the capacity of the bank to service SMEs. Of particular note, in April 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank introduced micro-credit technology and experience from Germany, and launched a new micro-credit product suitable for small businesses and privately or individually-owned businesses. "Beibu Gulf Micro-credit". With an enthusiastic market response and with rapid business development, by the end of 2010, 1708 micro loans were issued with the cumulative loans amounting to 400 million yuan.

2. The institution-building to serve the Beibu Gulf Economic Zone was fully implemented and the capacity to service the construction of the Beibu Gulf Economic Zone was significantly improved. According to the regulatory requirements of Guangxi Office, regarding CBRC on institution-building, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank researched and determined a 'three-step' institution-building strategy (zone firstly, inside the zone secondly, and then outside the zone) then, in a timely manner, seized this favorable opportunity for market development and continuously accelerated the pace of institution-building. First, the bank focused on strengthening the relocation and transformation of the original outlets in the urban area of Nanning. Currently, transformation and relocation have been completed for 32 outlets, establishing a good social image externally and effectively increasing brand influence. Second, the bank dedicated itself to providing a full range of financial services for the rapid development of the Beibu Gulf Economic Zone. First-tier branches were consecutively established in Guigang and Yulin. A coverage of 4 + 2 urban service network in the Beibu Gulf Economic Zone was successfully realized. Meanwhile, Baise Branch, Wuzhou Branch, Binyang Beibu Bay Village Bank and second-tier branches in Dongxing and Pingxiang were also under intense preparation.

### 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

3. A major breakthrough was achieved in cooperation in the same business and remarkable results were realized in funds introduced from external part of the zone for support of enterprise development in the zone. In 2010, with restrictions in loan growth, growth rate, and funding frequency, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank actively explored new ideas, sought for cooperation in the same business outside the zone, strove to break through bottlenecks, and continued to make a significant contribution to economic development in Guangxi, thus making remarkable achievements. On August 25, 2010, the Bank, as the leading bank and the agency bank, launched a 500 million yuan circulating fund syndicated loan for Guangxi Non-ferrous Metal Group Co., Ltd., with the positive participation of Shenzhen Development Bank; on October 18, the Bank, as the initiator, organized syndications with three other financial institutions, HSBC Bank, Shenzhen Development Bank and Hankou Bank, to lend 600 million yuan to Nanjing Sugar Industry Co., Ltd.

4. Several measures were adopted and new breakthroughs were achieved for diversification of the development model for various businesses. Firstly, the Bank vigorously expanded its capital business. In 2010, inter-bank borrowing fund accumulation achieved 541.876 billion yuan; fund operating income was 412 million yuan. Secondly, bill business continued steadily. On March 29, 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank established a bill business center which officially commenced business on May 18, 2010. In 2010, total bill business amounted to 56.645 billion yuan and bill business income amounted to 224 million yuan. Thirdly, the bank gradually built up the financial services brand. In 2010, the Bank issued a total of 16 financial products, totaling 3,066 billion yuan to establish the good brand image of "Beibu Bay Financial Management" and "Yingxinbao" and consolidated brand image through strong support of economic construction. Fourthly, the Bank vigorously opened up supply chain finance and successively granted credit to Dongfeng Liuzhou Motor and its 18 vendors, with total credit amounting to 932 million yuan to support the development of key industries of the region. Fifth, in terms of international business, the Bank has established good relationships through cooperation with 64 domestic and foreign financial institutions, including 32 national financial institutions in ASEAN. In 2010, settlement of international business amounted to 331.52 million USD. On December 29, 2010, the Bank successfully conducted the first RMB settlement business for cross-border trade, through this establishment of a good international image.

5. The Bank fully implemented human resource development mechanisms and achieved outstanding results in personnel training. First, the Bank set up the Training Institute of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank for Professional Managers, organized seminars for training outstanding leaders and jointly held training courses for senior business executive AFP training courses with Tsinghua University and gradually improved the talents training system to create a professional team. Second, the Bank improved the client / manager evaluation system, initially setting up corporate banking teams, retail banking, and micro-loan client manager teams of the Bank, enriched various lines of business and provided strong support for business marketing throughout the entire bank. Third, the Bank perfected performance evaluation tools, introduced FTP evaluation mechanisms, including into the scope of the assessment incomes of all departments, positions, and all cadres and giving full play to the leverage role of incentive. Fourth, the Bank improved relevant welfare systems, protected the basic rights of employees, and enhanced their sense of belonging, to build a competitive team of staff.

## III. Improving the overall risk management framework and further enhancing and consolidating the foundation of internal control.

In 2010, the Board of Directors continuously strengthened comprehensive risk management, with the risk management committee at the core. At the beginning of the year, the Risk Management Committee of the Board of Directors formulated the Guidance of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Risk Management for 2010, clarified the four risk management objectives and adopted specific measures clarifying the Bank's risk management objectives and focus in 2010, laying a sound foundation for risk management throughout the whole year. The Business Management identified risk management in 2010, with "basic annual management of risk lines" as the main line, with "value creation with risk management" as the concept, and with "laying a solid basis for risk control and innovating management measures" as the goal-oriented aim, guiding risk management of the Bank and promoting continued and steady development of the various businesses.

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

At the end of 2010, the balance of our Bank's various types of deposit was 34.156 billion yuan, loan balance was 17.205 billion yuan, with respective increases of 10.733 billion yuan and 3.87 billion yuan over the previous year, respectively, up by 45.8% and 29.03%. The term-end loan-to-deposit ratio was 50.4%; non-performing loan balance was 169 million yuan and non-performing loan ratio was 0.98%, respectively down by 33.94 million yuan and 0.54 percentage points compared with the end of the previous year. In terms of credit risk, the amount of non-performing loans and the non-performing loan ratio decreased; in terms of market risk, the interest rate in the second half increased with changes in interest rates imposing higher requirements on the Bank's portfolio and trading; in terms of operational risk, excepting certain risks in payment, settlement, credit and other business operations, there were no significant operational risk loss events or incidents during the report period; and in terms of liquidity risk, monitoring and management of liquidity ratio indicators performed well, generally maintaining good liquidity.

The main risk indicators of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in 2010 were: non-performing loan ratio 0.98%, decreased by 0.54% over 2009; provision coverage 217.71%, increased by 56.55% from 2009; capital adequacy ratio 16.98%, down by 5.34% over 2009; core capital margin was 16.29%, down by 4.87% compared with 2009; return on assets was 1.02%, an increase of 0.11% compared with 2009; capital profit rate 11.92%, increased by 5.08% compared with 2009; liquidity ratio 48.26%, down by 0.33% compared with 2009; core debt dependence 45.52%, down by 0.46% compared with 2009. With the exception of the core debt dependence among the aforesaid risk indicators failing to reach regulatory requirements, the remaining indicators meet the regulatory standards or the requirements of window guidance. Provision coverage increased and the anti-risk ability was further enhanced. Relevant profit margins increased, in connection with certain increases in the efficiency of capital investment and loan bargaining power within the reporting period. The capital adequacy ratio decreased rapidly, mainly because of business development, in particular the accelerated growth of investment with operating capital and high occupation of capital by risk assets. Overall, the capital adequacy ratio gradually decreased to a more reasonable range as the Bank's business gradually developed.

IV. Further improving and perfecting the three-meeting and one-layer governance framework, forming a sound organizational structure of corporate governance

(I) The Bank conducted differentiated authorization, further forming a three-meeting and one-layer framework of corporate governance.

in the first nair of 2010, China Banking Regulatory Commission officially approved the qualifications of our President. In May 2010, the Board of Directors held a meeting of the board in Shanghai, to study differentiated authorizations of Chairman of the Board and President, authorizing the Chairman of the Board, on behalf of the Board of Directors, to pursue operational management, and to authorize the President to preside over the daily operation of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank, to separate overall ownership and operation rights and separate the powers of management and supervision to maintain checks and balances. According to the authorization of the Board of Directors, the President exercises this work division and authorization through three Vice Presidents. The Management of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank fully discharged their duties and responsibilities in respect of the Bank's daily business activities. At this point, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank further formed a three-meeting and one-layer separated and balanced corporate governance framework. The General Meeting of Shareholders is the highest authority of the Bank and all shareholders exercise their rights through the General Meeting of Shareholders; the Board of Directors is responsible for the General Meeting of Shareholders making decisions on the Bank's major principles and policies, development planning, employment of senior management and income distribution, and does not interfere with the business of transaction; the Board of Supervisors is responsible for supervising the fulfillment of the duties of the Board of Directors and senior management and major issues of finance and operation; Management represented by the President, is responsible for the day to day operations of the bank by organizing the implementation of resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders and Board of Directors, and is responsible to the Board of Directors.

# 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

(II) The Board of Directors enhanced the management of directors' performance and the decision-making capacity of directors was significantly improved.

In 2010, the Board of Directors made considerable progress in the meeting process, holding four regular meetings, basically maintaining quarterly meetings and holding communications voting on four occasions, to significantly rationalize meeting frequency, thus reducing the provisionally approved matters. In 2010, the Board of Directors deliberated a total of 31 issues, involving supplement to capital, development strategy, institutional setting, finance budget and other aspects. Directors contributed efficient decision-making through their own expertise and rich experiences, gradually improving their familiarity with the works of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank.

In 2010, the Board of Directors especially strengthened the relevant works of the special committees under the Board of Directors. The Strategy Committee, the Related Party Transactions Committee, and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee held a total of four meetings during the year; the Risk Management Committee and Audit Committee held a total of two meetings during the year, providing strong referrals for decision to the Board of Directors. In 2010, since the qualifications of the Independent Directors additionally elected had not been approved by the regulatory authorities, the Independent Directors performed their duties according to the laws prevailing. Independent Directors attended all the annual general meetings of shareholders and board meetings and hosted all the meetings of the Related Party Transactions Committee and the Nomination and Remuneration Committee throughout the year. Also the Independent Directors presided over the assessment of senior management in the performance of their duties, successively conducted on-site research in newly-established branches, and proposed independent and constructive views at board meetings and meetings of special committees.

(III) The Bank issued subordinated debts, laying a foundation for supplementary capital.

According to the resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders, the Board of Directors organized the issuance of subordinated debts at the end of October 2010. The Board of Directors set up an issuance working team composed of executive directors, senior executives, and business units, hired four top domestic industry agencies for assistance, and authorized the issuance working team to deal with daily affairs. As the end of 2010, the Bank had completed due diligence, material collection, financial audit, credit rating, first draft of materials and other related works.

(IV) The Bank strengthened implementation capacity building, enforcement powers of resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders, and supervisory powers over the implementations of the management levels.

1. Implementation of the resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders In 2010, the Board of Directors convened two general meetings of shareholders, including one annual general meeting of shareholders and one interim general meeting of shareholders. The notice, convening, holding, and the voting procedures of the meetings are in line with the provisions of Company Law, the Articles of Association, and rules of procedure of our bank, thus ensuring that all shareholders have equal status and fully enjoy their rights, ensuring all shareholders' rights to information, rights to participate, and rights to vote on important matters of the bank, making the decision-making of our bank more scientifically based.

On April 23, 2010, the Board of Directors held the annual general meeting of shareholders in Nanning in 2009 according to the laws. The meeting deliberated and adopted nine resolutions, namely: (1) Adopted 2009 Annual Report of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd.; (2) Adopted the 2009 Annual Report of the Board of Supervisors of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd.; (3) Adopted the 2009 Annual Report of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd. (including Annual Financial Report) and agreed to a disclosure summary of the annual report in the Financial Times and to disclose the annual report on the website of the Bank; (4) Adopted the Report on Implementation of 2009 Comprehensive Operation and Financial Budget of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank; (5) Adopted the 2009 Annual Profits Distribution Plan of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd.; (6) Adopted the 2010 Comprehensive Business Plan; Financial Receipts and Expenditures Budget of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank; (7) Agreed to authorise Oceanwide Construction Holding Co., Ltd. to transfer 180 million shares of the Bank held therein to its parent company China Oceanwide Holdings Group; (8) Agreed to appointment of the Director of the Bank Ma Chaomei to serve as Director of Liuzhou City Commercial Bank concurrently; and (9) Agreed with the Measures of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank Co., Ltd. on Election of Directors (Trial).

### 广西北部湾银行 2010 年年报

Implementation: with regard to information disclosure; on April 28, 2010, the Board of Directors disclosed a summary of the annual report in the Financial Times and disclosed the full report on the Bank website. With regard to profit distribution, as of the end of 2010, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank had completed most of the resolutions regarding the distribution of profits to shareholders, except for those individual shareholders and previous corporate shareholders that could not be contacted and confirmed for historical reasons. With regard to the share transfer by Oceanwide, Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank had submitted materials to Guangxi Office, CBRC, in May 2010. According to current understanding, the Bank is still waiting for final approval from the China Banking Regulatory Commission.

On October 18, 2010, the Board of Directors held an interim general meeting of shareholders according to the laws. The meeting deliberated and adopted a total of three resolutions, namely: (1) Adopted the Resolution of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on the Initiation of Village Bank; (2) Adopted the Financing Planning of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank; and (3) Adopted the Resolution of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank on Issuance of Subordinated Debt.

Implementation: after the general meeting of shareholders; the Board of Directors immediately convened a meeting specifically for disposition of the implementation of resolutions of the general meeting of shareholders. With regard to the establishment of village bank, as of the end of 2010, the Bank had completed negotiations, site selection, recruitment of senior executives, reporting access, etc. It is expected that it will be opened officially in the first half of 2011. With regard to the issuance of subordinated debt, the foregoing part of the report explains the details.

2. The Bank enhanced supervision over executive powers of the business management.

In 2010, the Board of Directors, in strict accordance with the rules on implementation of resolutions, strictly required the management to report the implementations of resolutions to the Board of Directors according to various corresponding procedures. The Board of Directors organized monthly operational analysis meetings. The Chairman of the Board, on behalf of the Board of Directors, received the operational report of the business management.

(V) The Bank was in strict compliance with the Articles of Association and relevant regulations to convene meetings and comprehensively improved the meeting and resolution levels.

In 2010, the Bank convened 8 board meetings, including 4 regular meetings and 4 communication votes. The agendas and written proposals of the meetings of the Board were formulated prior to the meetings. The notice, convening, holding, and the voting procedures of the meetings are in line with the provisions of Company Law, Articles of Association, and the procedural rules of our bank. Directors of our bank can comply with the provisions of the relevant laws, regulations and the Articles of Association of the Bank and can express clear opinions on the items discussed in the best interests of the Bank and all shareholders; if they are unable to attend the board meetings in person, they can confer proxy voting to other directors in writing. Meetings are as follows:

On March 22, 2010, the Bank, by means of communication voting, held the 18th board meeting which deliberated and adopted: (1) The establishment of the first-tier branch of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in Guigang City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; (2) The establishment of the first-tier branch of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in Yulin City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; (3) The establishment of the first-tier branch of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in Baise City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region; (4) The establishment of the first-tier branch of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in Wuzhou City, Guangxi Zhuang Autonomous Region.

(VI) The Bank further strengthened controls regarding the management of related party transactions.

In 2010, Board of Directors, under the guidance of relevant laws, regulations and Articles of Association, established and improved the related party management system, related party transactions and other rules, following comprehensive, prudent and effective principles. At the same time, the Board of Directors authorized the Related Party Transactions Committee to approve significant related party transactions, shortened the approval measures and processes, strengthened controls regarding daily management, supervision and inspection of related party transactions, to proactively prevent risk in related party transactions, to ensure a healthy, smooth, and safe business. In 2010, the Bank had one significant related party transaction with shareholders holding 5% and more than 5% of shares: on September 14, 2010, the Bank granted credit of 340 million yuan to Liuzhou Iron & Steel Company Ltd. with a credit period of one year. Guangxi Liuzhou Iron & Steel (Group) Company, provided under a guarantee of joint and several liability. Guangxi Liuzhou Iron & Steel (Group) Company held 7.5% of shares in the Bank. 84% of the shares of Liuzhou Iron & Steel Company Ltd. were held by Guangxi Liuzhou Iron & Steel (Group) Company.

## V. Shortcomings of work of the Board of Directors

(i) The membership of the Board of Directors is incomplete and Independent Directors are missing. According to the Articles of Association of the Bank, the members of the Board of Directors are set at 15 people, including 3 independent directors. Currently, the Bank has 13 board members, but only 1 Independent Director.

(II) The Board of Directors needs to pay more attention to the report of the business management, to enable them to master operations in a timely manner and to better supervise the business activities of the bank.

(III) The Board of Directors needs to conduct special studies to enable a proactive response to the rapidly changing economic and financial situation, and improve decision-making efficiency and awareness.

(IV) Directors need to further deepen their understanding, through research into the Bank, in order to be able to fully put forward proposals suitable for the development of the Bank.

## VI. Profit distribution plan of 2010

(Submitted to a special committee for deliberation)

## VII. Work plan of Board of Directors for 2011

In 2011, the Board of Directors will continue to take the concept of scientific development as guidance, give full play to the role of leadership and decision making, support the work of management, strive to realize the sustained and rapid development of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank, and maintain the interests of shareholders and investors to the fullest extent.

(II) Continue to strengthen the duties and performance of the Independent Director. In 2010, the Board of Directors enhanced the investigation capacities of the Independent Director through the roles of evaluation and supervision by the Independent Director over business activities, to ensure the independent and scientific advice of Independent Director. Meanwhile, the Bank will arrange for the Independent Director to keep office hours in the bank to fulfill the due diligence requirements of the office of Independent Director.

(III) Further enhance management of investor relations. The Board of Directors will continue to regard the provision of efficient services for shareholders and investors as the central consideration and maximizing the value to shareholders and investors as the goal, further strengthen contact and communication with investors and shareholders, strengthen communication with the regulatory authorities, improve service awareness, service quality and levels of service, and strengthen management of investor relations, and to strive toward building an efficient and collaborative management system for investor relations to an internationally advanced level while further enhancing the good image of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank in the capital markets and to the public.

(IV) According to the Comprehensive Business Plan of Guangxi Beibu Gulf Bank for 2010 adopted by the General Meeting of Shareholders, the Bank will urge all operators to achieve their target levels and promote the rapid and healthy development of the various businesses of this Bank.

(V) Continue to issue subordinated debt and strive for successful issuance in 2011.

(VI) Start the preparations for listing and actively seek strategic investors with powerful assets, advanced management, and excellent personnel.

(VII) Establish an interview system for Chairman of the Board and Independent Director for business management, further strengthen the risk controls of the Board of Directors over business, intensify encouragement of the Board of Directors in relation to both business management issues, and ensuring the full implementation of resolutions of the General Meeting of Shareholders and Board of Directors.
